# Key Files and Concepts

The per-development index of this library's headline developments: one
bullet per landed development, grouped thematically under five headings
(Theory Core, Structures, Constructions, Concrete Instances, Applied
Programming — the grouping is by subject, not by directory: `Structure/Topos.v`
sits under Theory Core), each recording what was delivered, at what strength
(`eq_refl`, `≈`, `Cat` against `StrictCat`), what was measured and by what
criterion (universe binders and constraint blocks, axiom closure, dependency
closure, `Fail` probes and their kinds), and what was NOT delivered. Until
2026-09-09 this was the "Key Files and Concepts" section of CLAUDE.md; it was
moved here with every bullet unchanged because CLAUDE.md is loaded into every
session and had grown past a megabyte. Any `.v` header, commit message, plan
document or issue checkbox written before that date that refers to the
CLAUDE.md Key Files index, to a bullet or figure in it ("the CLAUDE.md
bullet", what "CLAUDE.md records" or "carries"), or to a count of occurrences
in CLAUDE.md, refers to the entries or the count in this file.
Cross-references inside bullets to a bullet "above" or "below" are relative
to the section order here, which is the original order.

Conventions. One bullet per development, appended under the heading its
sibling developments already sit under. Every figure in a bullet is a
measurement with its criterion stated; a claim that cannot be re-measured from
the sentence does not belong here. Read a file's bullet before editing the
file (`grep -n 'File.v' docs/INDEX.md` on the basename, since some bullets
spell paths relative to their section, then read that line): it records the
traps already met. About a third of the `.v` files head a bullet of their own
(just over 300 of 926 on 2026-09-09, counting distinct bold heads), so
absence is not a signal. An `Edit` that inserts a bullet has twice eaten the
heading that followed it, so check `grep -c '^- \*\*' docs/INDEX.md` and
`grep -c '^## ' docs/INDEX.md` before and after inserting; `make index-check`
(run by lefthook and CI) fails if the five `## ` headings are not all present
in order. Companion documents: docs/AXIOMS.md (the axiom audit),
docs/INHABITATION.md (which flagship results have a concrete in-tree
witness), docs/SIZE.md (size and foundations), docs/NOTATION.md.

## Theory Core
- **Theory/Category.v**: Defines categories with setoid hom-sets
- **Theory/Functor.v**: Functors preserve equivalence — with the §I.3/§I.5 closure and reflection results: `Full_Compose`/`Faithful_Compose`, and `faithful_reflects_monic`/`_epic` (a faithful functor reflects both cancellation properties), from which the concrete-category corollary in Theory/Concrete/Morphisms.v follows. Subcategory inclusions are faithful generically (`Incl_Faithful`, Construction/Subcategory.v); the converse "full inclusion ⟹ full subcategory" needs the selected morphisms to be closed under `≈`, which the `Subcategory` record does not supply and which Construction/Subcategory/FullConverse.v proves NECESSARY by counterexample
- **Theory/Shapes.v**: functors out of the walking shapes (Mac Lane §I.3) — objects ≃ functors `_1 ⟶ C` (`Point`/`point_of`), arrows ≃ functors `_2 ⟶ C` (`Walk`/`arrow_of`), composable pairs ≃ functors `_3 ⟶ C` (`Functor_of_Pair`), each an explicit construction pair with both round trips rather than a bijection class, the `_1` and `_2` ones landing at the strict `Functor_StrictEq_Setoid`. The category-level comparisons `One_Fun_iso : [_1, C] ≅[Cat] C` and `Two_Fun_Arrow : [_2, C] ≅[Cat] Arrow C` — both at `C : Category@{o Set Set}`, forced on the `_2` side because `Fun` identifies source and target hom universes while `_2`'s homs live in `Set` — close the gap `Construction/Arrow.v` previously disclosed as documentation-level — read their strength precisely: `≅[Cat]` is EQUIVALENCE, `Arrow_Fun_Arrow_strict` is strict on one side only, and the `StrictCat` isomorphism is explicitly not delivered (the object component would be a Leibniz equality of functor records, which `fmap_id` alone does not give). Seven Sketches instantiations: the three functors `_2 ⟶ _3` of Example 3.36 exhibited as named morphisms and proved pairwise non-equivalent, the six-functor count of Exercise 3.37 DERIVED by transporting the morphism count of `3` rather than enumerated, and Exercise 3.45's "functors from 1 to Sets are sets" turned from comment prose into a theorem. Note the name: the pre-existing `Instance/Shapes.v` is unrelated (its `Shape` indexes tries)
- **Theory/Diagram.v**: Diagrams and commutativity — a diagram in `C` of shape `G` is a quiver homomorphism `Diagram G C := QuiverHomomorphism G (QuiverOfCat C)`, path denotation `dpath` composes edge labels along a `tlist` path, and `Commutative D` quantifies over EVERY pair of vertices and EVERY pair of parallel paths of arbitrary length (Mac Lane §I.1, no shape privileged — unlike the tree's figure-fixing statements `Construction/Sq.v`'s `dsq`, `Structure/Cone.v`'s `cone_coherence`, and `Theory/Morphisms/Stability.v`'s `is_pullback_commutes`, the last two of which are recovered as instances). The bridge to the free category runs both ways with both round trips proved — `FunctorOfDiagram`/`DiagramOfFunctor`, `functor_of_diagram_of_functor` in StrictCat's hom-setoid and `diagram_of_functor_of_diagram` in `QuiverCategory` — and under it `Commutative` coincides with the Seven Sketches diagram-as-functor predicate `CommutativeShape` (`commutative_iff_shape`, `shape_iff_commutative`); respectfulness and naturality of the two maps are disclosed as NOT established, so the two maps are mutually inverse up to `≈` pointwise — weaker than a bijection of the underlying types (the round trips are up to `≈`, not `=`) and weaker than one of the setoid quotients (without respectfulness the maps do not descend), and in particular not a hom-setoid isomorphism. Walking square and triangle with the general predicate proved EQUIVALENT to the single two-composite equation (`square_commutative_iff`, `triangle_commutative_iff`), the naturality square as such a diagram (`naturality_square_commutative_iff`), Riehl's Lemma 1.6.20 for arbitrary path length (`faithful_reflects_commutative`), and the Solver-style term denotation `dterm` over `Construction/Free/Quiver.v`'s `Mor` with `dterm_dpath`/`commutative_dterm`. Concrete axiom-free witnesses in `Coq` escape BOTH vacuity traps, each escape proved: the shape genuinely has two distinct parallel paths (`sq_via_B_neq_via_C`, in Theory/Diagram.v) and the target is provably not thin (`coq_parallel_not_equiv`), so `coq_square_commutative` is not commuting by collapse — and `coq_square_not_commutative` is a provably NON-commuting diagram over the SAME quiver into the SAME category (Theory/Diagram/Examples.v). The empty path is not inert: `loop_commutative_iff` proves that over the walking loop `Commutative` is EXACTLY "the drawn endomorphism is `id`", with concrete `Coq` witnesses both ways (`coq_loop_negb_not_commutative`, `coq_loop_id_commutative`); the header is careful about what this separates — `dsq` quantifies over arbitrary OBJECTS, so `dsq X X X X e id id id` reduces to `e ≈ id` and CAN state the loop condition, the real distinction being that `Commutative` FORCES it from the shape alone (the empty path is always available as a competitor) while `dsq` must be instantiated to it, and `cone_coherence`/`is_pullback_commutes` are record FIELDS that cannot be freely instantiated at all. The two walking shapes are acyclic, proved by a rank argument (`sq_endo_paths_are_nil`, `tri_endo_paths_are_nil`) rather than inferred from empty self-edge sets — which would not suffice, a directed cycle of length ≥ 2 having no self-edge. The Seven Sketches footnote packaging (commutes ⟺ factors through the preorder reflection) IS proved, in both directions (`commutative_shape_factors`, `factors_commutative_shape`, `factors_commutative_shape'`, `commutative_factors`), and packaged as the single biconditional `commutes_iff_factors`, with the forward factorization an equality of FUNCTORS in StrictCat's hom-setoid (`shape_factor_functor`), over **Construction/PreorderReflection.v** — the preorder reflection as the quotient of a category by the TOTAL hom-congruence, `PreorderReflect C := Quotient C (TotalRel C)` with `preorder_reflect_thin` and the identity-on-objects `Reflect`, plus the universal property `ThinLift`/`ThinLift_proj`/`ThinLift_unique` showing every functor into a thin category factors through `Reflect` uniquely — so it is THE universal thin quotient, which is what earns the word "reflection" rather than an nLab pointer. This is NOT the nLab's *posetal* reflection, which identifies OBJECTS by mutual relatedness; `preorder_reflect_obj` proves objects are untouched definitionally. It needed no new machinery (`Construction/Quotient.v` already has the hom-congruence quotient and `QuotientLift`; all FOUR `HomCongruence` fields are immediate — reflexivity is the derived `cong_refl`, not a field), and it supplies work item 1 of issue #803's SEVEN, the other six remaining open; #803's plan supplies the module name and `PreorderReflect`, the other names being this file's own
- **Theory/Natural/Transformation.v**: Natural transformations — the arrows-only (object-free) presentation is Theory/Natural/Transformation/Arrows.v (Mac Lane §I.4 exercise 5): `ArrowTransform` indexes a morphism `S c ~> T c'` by each arrow `f : c ~> c'` under two splice laws, with the round trip to `Transform` (components `τ_arr id`) both ways, the four uniqueness statements, and the correspondence packaged as an `Isomorphism` in `Sets` between the two setoids. Two results worth knowing: respectfulness of the family in its arrow argument is DERIVABLE from the two laws rather than extra data (each law supplies one leg of the detour through `f ∘ id`), and the two splice laws are genuinely INDEPENDENT — `dom_family`/`cod_family`, indexed by the WALKING ARROW `_2` with the parallel-pair category as target (the target is what supplies the two non-equivalent arrows that separate; the index is where the domain and codomain of a non-identity arrow come apart), satisfy one law and refute the other, so neither field can be dropped. A closing section settles the companion question with countermodels over a hom-setoid that genuinely quotients: NEITHER law alone implies respectfulness (`left_law_alone_gives_no_respect`, `right_law_alone_gives_no_respect`), so the derivation's use of both laws is essential rather than an artifact of the proof. This is unlike `naturality`/`naturality_sym` in the parent file, which are one equation in two orientations
- **Theory/Adjunction.v**: The most important concept - adjunctions
- **Adjunction/Conjugate.v**: Mac Lane §IV.7 — conjugate natural transformations, the mate OPERATOR upgraded to the mate RELATION. `Conjugate A A' σ τ` IS the hom-set square `⌊k ∘ σ x⌋' ≈ τ a ∘ ⌊k⌋` quantified over every transposable `k`, not its value at one distinguished argument, with the inverse-transpose reading `ConjugateFrom` proved equivalent (`conjugate_iff_from`); `conjugate_characterizations` proves four pasting forms all equivalent to it — the two mate formulas `τ = U'ε ∘ U'σU ∘ η'U` and `σ = ε'F ∘ F'τF ∘ F'η`, which are what `mate`/`mate_inv` compute, and the unit and counit equations `τF ∘ η = U'σ ∘ η'` and `ε ∘ σU = ε' ∘ F'τ`, the counit equation having had no in-tree statement at all and the unit equation only the degenerate `F = F'` form of Theory/Bicategory/Adjunction.v's `mate_charac`/`mate_unit_compat`. Each transformation of left adjoints has one and only one conjugate and dually (`conjugate_unique_right`/`conjugate_unique_left`, by evaluating the square at the universal arrows ε and id), packaged as `conjugate_bijection : (F' ⟹ F) ≊ (U ⟹ U')` in Sets — the ordinary-category form of Theory/Bicategory/Mates.v's `mate_iso`, developed over arbitrary C and D in a seven-module cone with no bicategorical machinery (the Cat route stays available at any size, at the cost of Instance/Cat and the bicategory chain). Riehl §4.3(iv) rides it: `conjugate_invertible_iff` (σ pointwise invertible ⟺ its conjugate is) is proved from the square alone, using neither transformation's naturality, so Mates.v's descope ledger 10 was untouched by that file — `conjugate_id`/`conjugate_compose` are that ledger entry's identity-bounding-cell shadow, not its discharge, and the VERTICAL half of what `Instance/Adj/Bicategory.v` later completes horizontally, narrowing the note without discharging it. The bridge is Instance/Cat/Bicategory/Conjugate.v: padding transforms (`F' ◯ Id ⟹ Id ◯ F` is not `F' ⟹ F` definitionally, the two functor records carrying different `fmap_respects`/`fmap_id`/`fmap_comp` fields, which are data here and which record eta cannot identify), `Cat_conj_mate_agrees`/`Cat_conj_mate_inv_agrees` identifying `conj_mate`/`conj_mate_inv` with `mate`/`mate_inv` at identity bounding cells through the transparent `Cat_Adjunction_BicatAdjunction` rather than the Qed-opaque `Cat_BicatAdjunction_Adjunction_iff`, `conjugate_bijection_is_mate_iso`, equating the forward leg of `conjugate_bijection` with `mate_iso`'s forward leg conjugated by the two padding isomorphisms, the `Cat_mate_inv_unfold_raw` the tree lacked, and the boundary witness `mate_of_iso_not_invertible` — an invertible 2-cell whose mate over the non-identity bounding functor `Erase _2` is not invertible
- **Adjunction/Map.v**: Mac Lane §IV.7 definition 1 and Proposition 1 (book p. 99) + Riehl §4.2 Exercise 4.2.v (printed p. 143) — **maps of adjunctions, delivered in BOTH the strict and the `≈` reading over ONE engine that needs neither**. The engine is `Section MapCompare`: an arbitrary pair of comparison ISOMORPHISM families `al : ∀ x, K (F x) ≅ F' (L x)` and `be : ∀ a, L (U a) ≅ U' (K a)`, over which `MapAdjHom`/`MapAdjUnit`/`MapAdjCounit` are stated and the three-way equivalence is proved ONCE (`map_adj_hom_iff_unit`, `map_adj_hom_iff_counit`, `map_adj_unit_iff_counit`). **The naturality hypotheses are EXPLICIT ARGUMENTS, so each passage's TYPE records what it consumes** — measured, not asserted: `map_hom_to_unit` and `map_hom_to_counit` consume NEITHER square's naturality, `map_unit_to_hom` only the RIGHT, `map_counit_to_hom` only the LEFT. **BOTH READINGS ARE INSTANTIATIONS OF THAT ENGINE, AND THEY ARE NOT PARALLEL CONSTRUCTIONS**: the strict `Record AdjSquares` (Leibniz object equations `sq_left`/`sq_right` plus their naturality, with the hom-set condition written through `id_cast`) and the `≈` `Record WeakAdjSquares` (fields `wsq_left : wsq_K ◯ F ≈ F' ◯ wsq_L`), related by **`strict_hom_is_weak_hom : SquaresHom A A' S = WeakSquaresHom (WeakAdjSquares_of_AdjSquares S)` at LEIBNIZ EQUALITY OF TYPES by `reflexivity`**, so `WeakMapOfAdjunctions_of_MapOfAdjunctions` carries `map_hom` across unchanged with no proof. `SquaresHom` is quantified over EVERY `x : D`, `a : C` and `k : F x ~> a` — the issue's explicit reviewer check — and `map_of_adjunctions_unit_iff_counit` and `MapOfAdjunctions` are its two pinned names. **THE ISSUE IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT ON THE MODELLING DECISION AND BOTH ITS HALVES ARE DELIVERED, SO NOTHING OF IT IS REFUTED — what IS refuted is the COORDINATOR'S OBJECTION, and the file says which.** Its Work item 1 asks for "the two strict commutation equations for the functor squares" and its Work item 4 calls the notion "the strict special case", while its modelling note directs "Deliver the `≈` version (which is the usable one)"; both readings are delivered and the decision is disclosed, which is what its Definition of Done actually asks. Strict is primary here on source fidelity, both books stating the definition strictly (Riehl's exercise is titled "**strict** morphism of adjunctions", writes `KF = F′H`, and joins her display with `═`; Mac Lane's display (3) uses a double bar `‖`), so strict is primary here and the `≈` version rides alongside. The coordinator's brief had claimed the `≈` condition "does not even typecheck without transport"; the OBSERVATION is right about the naive spelling (pinned as the probe's TYPING negative 1) but the CONCLUSION is wrong — a `Functor_Setoid` equality supplies exactly the isomorphism family the engine wants, and inserting `from (al x)`/`to (be a)` makes the condition well typed with NO transport at all. **The identity-bounding-functor case IS `Adjunction/Conjugate.v`, ON THE NOSE**: `map_adj_hom_is_conjugate : MapAdjHom A A' Id[C] Id[D] al be = Conjugate A A' conj_sigma conj_tau` by `reflexivity`, again Leibniz equality of TYPES, and **no padding transformation is needed** — `Id`'s object and arrow actions are the literal identities, so the `F' ◯ Id` trap `Instance/Cat/Bicategory/Conjugate.v` records is bicategorical and does not arise on this route. **SCOPE THAT IDENTIFICATION EXACTLY**: a map of adjunctions supplies INVERTIBLE comparison data while `Conjugate σ τ` demands no invertibility of either transformation, so what is recovered is a conjugate pair whose two transformations are POINTWISE INVERTIBLE, and not every conjugate pair arises this way — pinned as a TYPING negative; the converse, that every pointwise-invertible conjugate pair does arise, is NOT built (no constant in the file takes an `IsIsomorphism`-family hypothesis), so only the one inclusion is machine-checked (a bare `Transform` does not inhabit the iso family), with `Conjugate.v`'s own `conjugate_invertible_iff` recording that the two invertibility conditions imply each other under the square. **The issue's Current-state section is stale in what it OMITS rather than in what it asserts**: its clause "no lemma writes either the unit condition or the counit condition" is TRUE as scoped, since `ConjugateUnit` and `ConjugateCounit` quantify over no `K` or `L` at all and Mac Lane's conditions `Lη = η'L` and `ε'K = Kε` are about a bounding functor — what the issue misses is that `Adjunction/Conjugate.v` exists at all, naming `Theory/Bicategory/Mates.v` as "the nearest relative" though Conjugate.v is the SAME section of the SAME book and is exactly this file's identity-bounding-functor case; and `Instance/Adj.v`'s own caveat block already names `Conjugate` as Mac Lane's §IV.7 hom-set square; that file is UNTOUCHED and its proposed hom retyping is a declined follow-on. Mac Lane's literal displays are `squares_unit_fused`/`squares_counit_fused` (`Lη = η'L`, `Kε = ε'K` with the whole identification on one side). Identity and composition exist (`AdjSquares_id`, `AdjSquares_compose`, `MapOfAdjunctions_id`, `MapOfAdjunctions_compose`, with `eq_refl` readbacks for both object actions), but **NO associativity or unit law is stated and the unit law is REFUTED at `eq_refl` and pinned** — `AdjSquares_compose` builds `sq_K M ◯ Id[C]`, not `sq_K M` — so there is no category or 2-category of adjunctions here; stating a law up to `≈` would first need a setoid on maps, which is not built. Two `id_cast` lemmas absent from `Construction/Quotient.v` are stated here and disclosed as belonging beside their donors (`id_cast_sym_trans`, `fmap_id_cast_sym`). **The squares are written in `id_cast` form rather than through `Functor_StrictEq_Setoid` on a MEASURED ground**: requiring `Theory/Skeleton.v`, where `strict_equiv_of_id_cast_nat` lives, takes the closure from **21 to 32** modules; the PROBE pays that once and proves the record's fields ARE that constant's arguments by application alone, with no tactic and no transport. - **Adjunction/Parameter.v**: Mac Lane §IV.7 Theorem 3 with its remark and Exercise 2 (book pp. 101–102, `maclane:IV.7:thm3`/`remark1`/`ex2`) + §IX.4 Ex 2 (`maclane:IX.4:ex2`) + Riehl §4.4 Proposition 4.4.6 and Exercise 4.4.ii (`riehl:4.4:prop6`, `riehl:4.4:exii`) — **adjunctions with a parameter: the right adjoints of a bifunctor's partial functors extend UNIQUELY to a bifunctor contravariant in the parameter, with the bijection natural in all three variables**. `Record ParametrizedAdjunction (F : X ∏ P ⟶ A)` carries `pa_right : P → (A ⟶ X)` and `pa_adj (p) : Partial_l F p ⊣ pa_right p`, and **`parametrized_right_adjoint_bifunctor : P^op ∏ A ⟶ X`** is Mac Lane's `G` (both names are the issue's pinned ones, delivered verbatim). **THE FUNCTORIALITY IS CONSUMED FROM #394, NOT RECOMPUTED, WHICH IS WHAT THE THEOREM ACTUALLY SAYS**: `pa_param_mate` is `conj_mate` and nothing else (`pa_param_mate_is_conj_mate`, `eq_refl`), `pa_param_mate_id` ends `apply conj_mate_id` and `pa_param_mate_comp` ends `apply conj_mate_compose` — both of those donors being themselves proved by `apply conj_mate_uniq` — so Mac Lane's "the uniqueness of the choice of conjugates shows for `h'h` that `G(h'h,−) = G(h,−) ∘ G(h',−)`, so that `G(−,a)` is a functor and `G` a bifunctor" is discharged BY NAME; a donor-use census over the file gives `conj_mate_uniq` 5, `conj_mate` 4, `conj_mate_respects` 3, `conj_mate_id` 3, `conj_mate_compose` 3, `conjugate_iff_from` 2, `conjugate_unique_right` 1, `conjugate_conj_mate` 1, and no conjugacy is re-derived anywhere. **`pa_square_is_Conjugate` closes at `eq_refl` ON THE TYPES**, so his "must be chosen as the conjugate to `F(−,h)`" is true by construction rather than by argument, with `pa_square_from_is_ConjugateFrom` the inverse-transpose twin and `pa_square_iff_from` a `:=` of `conjugate_iff_from`. THE BOOK: "(a) For monads ⟨T, η, μ⟩ and ⟨T', η', μ'⟩ on X, define a morphism θ of monads as a suitable natural transformation θ : T ⇝ T', and construct the category of all monads in X. (b) From θ construct a functor θ* : X^{T'} → X^T such that G^T ∘ θ* = G^{T'} and a natural transformation F^T ⇝ θ* ∘ F^{T'}." Part (a) repeats the close of §VI.1 (p. 139: "We leave the reader to describe a morphism ⟨T, μ, η⟩ → ⟨T', μ', η'⟩ of monads (a suitable natural transformation T ⇝ T') and the category of all monads in a given category X"), and two other pages give Mac Lane's own answer: p. 138, "All told, a monad in X is just a monoid in the category of endofunctors of X", and §VII.3, p. 171, "A morphism f : ⟨c, μ, η⟩ → ⟨c', μ', η'⟩ of monoids is an arrow f : c → c' such that fμ = μ'(f □ f) … fη = η'. With these arrows, the monoids in B constitute a category Mon_B", its table pairing ⟨C^C, ∘, Id⟩ with "Monads (cf. Chapter VI!)"; so his category of all monads in X is Mon_{X^X}. - **Monad/Eilenberg/Moore/Limit.v**, **Monad/Eilenberg/Moore/Limit/Examples.v** (probe `Test/ProbeEMCreates467.v`): Mac Lane §VI.2 Exercise 2, "Show that G^T : X^T → X creates limits" (book p. 142, PDF p. 151; `maclane:VI.2:ex2`), read with the unnumbered Definition of §V.1 (book p. 112, PDF p. 121), both from the page images, issue #467 — **`EM_Forget T` strictly creates every limit, for every monad T on every category: clause (i)'s existence at `eq_refl` (the apex, the transport `slift_eq`, and each leg against the GIVEN cone), clause (i)'s "exactly one pair" at `≈` only (`em_alg_unique` at the pinned carrier, and `em_lift_alg_unique`, new in #467, at the carrier of any `StrictLift`: an isomorphism in `EilenbergMoore T` to the created apex lying over `slift_iso`, instantiated at `Sets` by `em_lift_alg_unique_Sets` in Examples.v, at an indiscrete carrier where its `≈`-conclusion holds of every map, so that the instance witnesses the premise, a strict lift other than the created one), its on-the-nose form REFUTED without axioms (`em_lift_not_unique_leibniz`, and `em_limiting_lift_not_unique_leibniz` among limiting lifts), clause (ii) as `em_created`, and reflection (`em_reflects`) beyond the book**. THE BOOK: "A functor V: A → X creates limits for a functor F: J → A if (i) To every limiting cone τ: x →· VF in X there is exactly one pair ⟨a, σ⟩ consisting of an object a ∈ A with Va = x and a cone σ: a →· F with Vσ = τ, and if, moreover, (ii) This cone σ: a →· F is a limiting cone in A." STATE BEFORE #467, measured: the mathematics had shipped with #406 (commit bdce5ebe, PR #1083), both files added there — `em_created`, `em_alg_unique`, `em_reflects`, `em_strict_lift`, `em_forget_StrictlyCreatesLimit(s)`, `em_forget_CreatesLimit`, `em_forget_CreatesAllLimits`, `EM_Complete` and the hypothesis-free instance at `Id_Monad` over `Coq`; the issue's "Current state" (no theorem that `EM_Forget` creates or even preserves limits) was accurate when the issue was filed (2026-07-23) and has been stale since PR #1083 (#406, commit bdce5ebe), on which #467 was filed as depending, merged on 2026-08-13 (the issue's createdAt and the pull request's mergedAt, by `gh issue view` and `gh pr view`), and the sentence occurs in the tree only in its archived draft, doc/plan/books/maclane/issues/VI-drafts.md, left unchanged (a grep of the `.v` and `.md` files for it); Limit.v's header cited §VI.2 Theorem 1 (p. 140, the adjunction) and never Exercise 2, now corrected in place with a clause-by-clause map (CORRECTION (#467)); the files had no bullet of their own, Limit.v being named in four others (Structure/Limit.v's, as the witness; Instance/Grp/Limit.v's, for the architecture it shares; Instance/Ab/Limit.v's, for two renamed collisions; Instance/Mod/TensorMonad.v's, as the limit clause at `EM_Forget`; a grep of docs/INDEX.md); and 2 of their 49 constants (Limit.v 43, Examples.v 6, by `Print Module`) were gated by name, `em_forget_CreatesAllLimits` and `EM_Complete` by short name (a grep of the Makefile for each name under any qualifier). STRENGTHS, each restated in the probe: at `eq_refl`, the apex (C1), the transport, which IS `eq_refl` (C4), each leg against the given cone, directly, through the class projection `screates` and as the leg family (C2, C2b, C3), the structure map as the mediator of the action cone (C5), the forward map of `creates_lift_over`'s iso as `id` (C6), and the created limit's legs (C7); the image cone as a RECORD against the given cone is refused (R1, "cannot unify"), on its coherence field alone, since rebuilding it with the given cone's coherence field is `eq_refl` to that cone (C8), its CAUSE STRUCTURAL, argued and not flip-measured (an application of `fcone_coherence`, a `Qed` lemma whose body is a rewrite chain over D's abstract hom-setoids, against a stuck projection of the variable N). The class form of the uniqueness clause is Structure/Limit/Creation.v's `screates_lift_unique` at `em_forget_StrictlyCreatesLimit T K`, a cone isomorphism to the created lift from any cone whose image is cone-isomorphic to N; `em_lift_alg_unique` specialises it to a `StrictLift` and names the underlying map of the isomorphism, ≈ the transport, its type an isomorphism of algebras without the cone compatibility a `ConeIso` carries. The labels C1–C8, C2b, R1 and E1–E7 are mapped to the probe's constants in its LABELS paragraph (E4 `p467_e4_iso`: `em_lift_alg_unique_Sets` is `em_lift_alg_unique` at the example by `eq_refl`; E5: its underlying map is `id` by `eq_refl`). THE REFUTATION (Examples.v): at `Sets` with the identity monad `IdSM`, the indiscrete two-point setoid `Bool2` carries the two structure maps id and const true (`A_id`, `A_true`, distinct by `A_id_ne_A_true`, proved by a `match` on the equation, with no Eqdep and no UIP); over the shape `1`, the limiting cone `N1` (`N1_limiting`) has two lifts with apex equation `eq_refl` and legs EQUAL to `N1`'s (`lift1_at`, `leg_id_from`), both limiting (`lift1_limiting`), with different apexes; the two theorems quantify τ over the limiting cones, as the book's clause (i) does. This is a feature of the setoid encoding, not of Mac Lane's statement: for him, over any X, a T-algebra is a pair ⟨x, h⟩ with h an arrow of X (p. 140), arrows are compared by equality, and the universal property determines h, where here it determines the structure map only up to the carrier's `≈`, which on `Bool2` identifies every two maps; the statements' `=` between morphisms is the disclosed exception to the house rule, being the thing refuted. UNIVERSES, by `About`: `em_lift_alg_unique@{o h jo eo e l l0}` with h < e and the chain jo, h ≤ l0 ≤ l, o ≤ l, o, h ≤ eo, and only the sigma projections' two caps; a draft that rewrote under `fmap` carried three `prod_rect` caps and a phantom level, and one that used `subst` an `EqdepFacts` cap; Examples.v's seventeen new constants bind `@{o so}` of `Sets@{o so}` (`Bool2@{o p}` its setoid levels), plus `j` for the shape `1` and `l l0` for `IsLimitCone`, with the strict bound o < so and caps inherited from `Sets` (compose, ID), `_1` (eq_ind, eq_ind_r, Logic_lemmas.equality) and `EilenbergMoore` (the sigma projections); the monad is `IdSM`, built with every field given, not the library's `Id_Monad` (Monad/Strong.v), whose universe list has 3 levels on Rocq 9.1.1, 5 on Coq 8.20.1 and 17 on 8.19.2 (by the "Universe instance length" refusals of an explicit instance), so that no explicit instance compiles on all three, and which, left implicit, Coq 8.20.1 refuses under these binders ("Universe … is unbound" at `EMS`), measured on the overlays below; `K1` gives every functor field because `refine` resolves an open respectfulness field by an instance at `Set` and collapses o to `Set`, and `A_id_ne_A_true` reads its last equation at `bool` before `discriminate` to avoid an `eq_ind` cap of its own. - **Theory/Universal/Element.v**: Mac Lane §III.1 def 2 + remark 3 — UNIVERSAL ELEMENTS as a first-class structure, replacing the anonymous sigma `{ x : F c & IsIsomorphism (from (Yoneda_Lemma C F c) x) }` that `Structure/UniversalProperty.v`'s `representability_by_yoneda` had buried inside one proposition. `UniversalElement H` (bundled) and `AUniversalElement H r` (object as parameter) carry Mac Lane's elementary unique-factorization form, with setoids comparing the underlying element. Deliverable 2 is stated at the strength it actually has: **an isomorphism of setoids in `Sets`** (`universal_element_yoneda`), not a biconditional and not mutually inverse maps up to `≈` — and it is free of transport because `ue_yoneda_obj` is `representability_by_yoneda`'s source TERM FOR TERM (the same `#[local] exists_setoid` constant, reachable by qualified name and re-registered locally; `rby_agrees` checks the match by ascription). Had a copy been re-declared instead, the two `SetoidObject`s would not have been convertible and a hand-built comparison iso would have been needed — worth knowing for anyone else composing with that proposition. The equivalence's grades are measured, not assumed: the mate's ACTION is definitional (`ue_mate_at` by `reflexivity`, so Mac Lane's `(H k) e` and the Yoneda mate's component are the same term), the passage OUT of the Yoneda encoding costs 2 obligations, and the passage IN costs 5 (the inverse must be built as a natural transformation, and each naturality square is a uniqueness argument through `fmap_comp`) — so the cheap direction is out, not in. Round trips survive on the ELEMENT by `eq_refl` both ways; the whole record does not (factorization data is rebuilt), pinned as a `Fail`. Mac Lane's remark 3 is ONE theorem, `universal_element_arrow_subsumption`, carrying both halves — (a) universal elements of `H` are universal arrows from the one-point setoid `SetsOne`, and (b) `⟨r,u⟩` is a universal arrow from `c` to `S` iff it is a universal element of `d ↦ Hom(c, S d)` — with `subsumption_composite` the round trip that exists only once both halves do. Half (b) is much the cheaper: the two records' field types are CONVERTIBLE (`fmap[[Hom c,─] ◯ S] k u` IS `fmap[S] k ∘ u`), so both passages are `:=` with no tactic and both round trips are `eq_refl` on the WHOLE record; half (a) reaches only `≈` on the arrow side, `global_element` rebuilding the map from its value at `ttt`. **A DONOR UNIVERSE RESTRICTION drove the design and is disclosed rather than worked around silently**: `Yoneda_Lemma@{u u0}` and `representability_by_yoneda@{u u0}` are stated over `C : Category@{u0 u0 u0}` — object, hom AND proof universes IDENTIFIED — so neither can be instantiated at `Instance/Coq/Nat.v`'s `Endos`, whose objects sit strictly above its homs, and the Nat witness would not have existed by that route. - **Adjunction/GAFT/Necessity.v**, **Instance/Ordinal/Large.v**: Mac Lane §V.6 (book pp. 122-123) with Awodey §9.8 Remark 9.30 — **the solution set condition is necessary, and the size discipline that makes it necessary is measured rather than described**. The abstract half is three facts about the constant functor at the singleton, `ConstOne C : C ⟶ Sets`: it is **continuous for every `C` with no hypothesis at all** (the proof ignores its is-a-limit-cone argument, so it proves the stronger statement that EVERY cone maps to a limit cone); it is **representable exactly when `C` has an initial object** (`ConstOne_representable_iff_initial`, both directions — `Hom(c,−) ≅ ConstOne` says every hom-set out of `c` is a singleton, which IS initiality, and `Initial C` is notation for `@Terminal (C^op)`); and therefore over any `C` that is complete-for-small-shapes with no initial object, `ConstOne C` is continuous and not representable, which is the sharpness of #437's `representability_theorem` and of GAFT itself. **The deep point is a universe measurement, and an earlier revision of the header got it backwards.** That revision said the library's `Complete` has "no smallness side condition", hence `@Complete C` already yields `@Initial C`, hence "complete with no initial object" is an EMPTY pair and the counterexample "cannot be stated over `@Complete`". Measured, that overstates a real fact into a false one. `Complete` DOES carry the side condition — the shape's object universe strictly below the ambient's, stated in terms at `Instance/Sets/Complete.v` — and `Complete_Initial` consumes the COLLAPSED instance, i.e. large-completeness. Applying it to each witness in the tree: `Sets_Complete`, `Grp_Complete`, `Ab_Complete` and `SmallOrd_op_Complete` are all **refused**; exactly one is **accepted**, the thin `Subsets_Complete` (`Instance/Powerset.v`). That is Freyd's collapse (`Structure/Complete/Freyd.v`) appearing as a universe constraint — a category with limits over shapes as large as itself has an initial object and is a preorder — so the four `Complete_*` constants are statements about large-completeness, inert on every large category in tree, and the file says so instead of leaving a reader to find out. **Which is exactly why the counterexample must live at small-completeness**, and `Instance/Ordinal/Large.v` is built to sit there. Its ordinals are the Aczel/W-type `osup : ∀ I : Type@{u}, (I → SmallOrd@{u}) → SmallOrd@{u}` with `SmallOrd@{u} : Type@{u+1}`, and the file delivers **the same library class inhabited at one universe instance and refuted at another over one and the same category**: `SmallOrd_op_Complete : Complete@{u u Set u0}` with `u < u0` against `SmallOrd_op_not_large_complete : @Complete SmallOrd_op_Proset → False` at the diagonal instance, with `SmallOrd_self_limit : Limit (Id[SmallOrd_Proset])` as the control proving the diagonal pairing is not uninhabitable in general (its `Limit@{u u1 u0 u1}` has slots 2 and 4 identified, the very pairing the refutation kills on the other side). **Two pieces of the plan were wrong and the construction corrected them**: `osup I f` is NOT the least upper bound of the `f i` — it is the sup of their SUCCESSORS, and `smallord_lub_not_zero` refutes the naive reading — so the LUB is the flattening `ojoin` over the dependent sum of index types, still at `Type@{u}`; and the `≤`/`<` mutual fixpoint the plan proposed cannot pass the guard checker, since `ole` recurses on its first argument and `olt` would recurse on its second, so `ole` is single-argument structural and `olt` a plain definition. **And the universe argument is not where it was expected**: no-greatest-element needs no universe reasoning at all (successors exist, so `SmallOrd_no_greatest` is three lines from `olt_irrefl`); what the level gap buys is the COMPATIBILITY of small-completeness with the absence of a top, recorded as `SmallOrd_no_small_cofinal_family` — no `Type@{u}`-indexed family is cofinal, so `ojoin` provably cannot be applied to the class of all ordinals. Measured: **70 constants gated and all "Closed under the global context"** (7815 → 7885) — 29 `.glob` heads + 1 `Program` obligation for `Necessity.v`, 40 + 0 for `Large.v`. The Solovay half is a stated HYPOTHESIS, not an axiom: complete Boolean algebras are absent from the tree (the single tree-wide hit for solovay/complete boolean/CABA is a prose citation of a DIFFERENT Solovay result at `Instance/FdVect/NoRightAdjoint.v`), so the premise "no free complete Boolean algebra on a countable set exists" is a hypothesis of the theorem and the set-theoretic input is visible as such. Traps: `I` is the Prelude's constructor of `True`, so `match x with osup I f => …` reads `I` as a pattern variable shadowing it; and the three `Universes o h.` blocks in `Necessity.v` are KEPT but are **not** load-bearing — removing all three still compiles, because `Lib.v` sets `Unset Universe Minimization ToSet` project-wide, and an earlier header revision crediting them is corrected. Not delivered: `SmallOrd_Proset` is NOT shown to fail `Small` — the largeness here is a universe-LEVEL fact and refuting `Small` needs non-resizability, a separate argument close to Burali-Forti — so the Awodey hidden checkbox is met in the vocabulary of universe instances rather than of `Theory/Size.v`; no antisymmetry, trichotomy, well-foundedness or ordinal arithmetic, `ole` being claimed only as a preorder; no comparison with `Instance/Omega.v`'s ω or `Instance/Ordinal.v`'s finite ordinals; and no refutation probe under `Test/`, so the two universe-instance boundaries are measured but not guarded.

- **Lib/Setoid/Propositional.v**, **Instance/Sets/Propositional.v**, **Test/ProbePropEquiv.v**: **a setoid whose equality is logically a PROPOSITION — the property, its transports, and the reason it is a property rather than a redefinition** (the PR "algebraic carriers are sets", 2026-09-17, its first phase). `Class PropEquiv@{u p} {A : Type@{u}} (S : Setoid@{u p} A) := { pequiv : A → A → Prop; pequiv_to : ∀ x y, pequiv x y → x ≈ y; pequiv_from : ∀ x y, x ≈ y → pequiv x y }` (`Lib/Setoid/Propositional.v`), measured by `About` under `Set Printing Universes` at `PropEquiv@{u p} : Setoid@{u p} A → Type@{max(Set+1,u,p)}` — AT the carrier universe for every `Setoid@{u u}`, which is the entire point: a `Prop`-valued relation on a carrier in `Type@{u}` is itself a type in `Type@{u}` while a `Type`-valued one lands in `Type@{u+1}`. That arithmetic is stated once and authoritatively in the size note in the header of `Structure/Complete.v`; this file is its implementation, and any disagreement is to be resolved in that note's favour. **`≈` IS NOT CHANGED, ANYWHERE**: `Class Setoid`'s `equiv` stays a `crelation` (`Lib/Setoid.v`), because in `Cat` an `F ≈ G` is a family of isomorphisms (`Theory/Functor.v`) and truncating it would discard data — `Test/ProbePropEquiv.v` pins that `Functor_Setoid` has no such `Prop` mirror, that a GENERIC `X : SetoidObject` supplies none either, and records why there is no `LocallyPropositional Sets`. **The three fields are FUNCTIONS, so no `Prop` is eliminated to build one**: `pequiv_to`/`pequiv_from` convert both ways, and the single elimination the property buys is `pequiv_elim_inhabited : inhabited (x ≈ y) → x ≈ y`, which is what makes every propositional truncation in the PR reversible at a propositional carrier. Constructor and instances: `PropEquiv_of_relation` for a setoid whose `equiv` IS a named `Prop` relation — the sort ascription `(x ≈ y : Prop)` is REFUSED even when `≈` is `eq`, since Coq judges the sort of `equiv x y` from the declared type of `equiv` (a negative with its own control) — together with instances for every setoid constructor of `Lib/Setoid.v`: `eq`, `unit`, `Fin`, `nat`, the pointwise function setoid, product, sum, option, list. `Instance/Sets/Propositional.v` transports the property through `Sets`: `PropEquivObj`, the hom-setoid pointwise into the target (`hom_PropEquiv`), binary products, indexed products (`iprod_PropEquiv`) and the vertex of `Instance/Sets/Complete.v`'s limit (`limit_PropEquiv`), each with an `eq_refl` readback that `pequiv` is the pointwise relation; and it declares `Class LocallyPropositional C := ∀ x y, PropEquiv (@homset C x y)` with the two generic builders `LocallyPropositional_of_relation` and `LocallyPropositional_of_eq`. **Measured on 2026-09-17**, criteria stated: 66 `.v` files mention `PropEquiv` (`grep -rl --include='*.v' PropEquiv .`); NINE constants inhabit `LocallyPropositional` (`grep -rn --include='*.v' -E '(Program )?(Definition|Instance) [A-Za-z_0-9]*_?LocallyPropositional' .`) — `Grp`, `Ab`, `CMon`, `RMod R`, a delooped rig, `Matr R`, the two generic builders, and the one the reverse direction of `Construction/Enriched/Ab.v` PRODUCES; and every constant of both files is "Closed under the global context" and gated. **SCOPE, deliberately narrow**: `PropEquiv` is a property of a SETOID and never of `Class Setoid`; internal algebra in an arbitrary category (the `Theory/Algebra/` files) keeps the ambient `≈` and carries no such field; and where an arbitrary category's hom-setoid must be read as an algebraic object, `LocallyPropositional` is taken as a HYPOTHESIS — it is never a theorem about `Sets` or about `Cat`, and neither is one (since #469 the blanket property is characterized: a `PropEquiv` on every object of `Sets` at once is interderivable with ∀ A, inhabited A → A at the carriers' level, Instance/Pos/Monadicity.v's `all_PropEquiv_trunc` and `trunc_all_PropEquiv`, a principle that informative excluded middle supplies and that has no axiom-free proof, argued there by normal forms; Instance/Sets/Propositional.v's header carries the same note as CORRECTION (#469), and the #469 bullet under Concrete Instances has the detail)

## Structures (Internal Properties)
- **Structure/Thin.v**: Thin categories — `Thin C := ∀ x y (f g : x ~> y), f ≈ g`, closed under opposites, with every morphism monic and epic and every opposing pair an iso candidate (`thin_iso`); `thin_preorder C` (inhabited-hom on objects, Prop-squashed; deliberately renamed to avoid shadowing `Theory/Category.v`'s exported Type-valued `hom_preorder` instance, which is the formulation that would dissolve the choice hypothesis — the squash is forced by `Instance/Proset.v`'s Prop-valued `Proset`) with its `PreOrder` witness (a plain `Definition`, deliberately not an instance). The thin-side reconstruction `thin_Proset_iso : Thin C → HomChoice C → C ≅[Cat] Proset (thin_PreOrder C)` takes the morphism-choice hypothesis explicitly (extracting a witness from the Prop-valued ∃ needs it; on prosets it is discharged, homs being the relation itself). Mac Lane §I.2 construction 7's correspondence, with strengths measured per leg in Instance/Proset/Order.v: `thin_preorder_Proset` recovers the relation pointwise-iff unconditionally, and on the nose (`thin_preorder_Proset_eq`) under propositional+functional extensionality taken as explicit hypotheses (sufficiency is what is proved; necessity is not claimed)
- **Structure/Complete/Freyd.v**: Mac Lane §V.2 Proposition 3 (book p. 114, `maclane:V.2:prop3`) + Awodey §9.8 Proposition 9.34 (`awodey:9.8:prop34`) + Riehl §3.7 Proposition 3.7.3 and Epilogue §E.1 (`riehl:3.7:prop3`, `riehl:E.1:thm-large-products-poset`; Definition 3.7.2, `riehl:3.7:def2`, is the size measure the proposition is stated against, consumed here as an ORDER and NOT delivered as a cardinal — its checkbox is not met as written) — **Freyd's collapse: a category whose arrows are indexed by a type at which it has products, and whose hom-setoids are decidable, is thin; and a product is a greatest lower bound in the preorder reflection of any category**. The smallness witness is `ArrowIndex C` (a type `ai_index` encoding every arrow, decoded RELATIVE TO A DEFAULT with the round trip the identity up to `≈` for every default — `|hom x y| ≤ |ai_index|` on every inhabited hom-set, Riehl's cardinality form, so LARGE categories are covered and her §3.7 stronger-hypothesis checkbox is met); Theory/Size.v's `Small` is deliberately not consumed (per-hom resizing through `ObjEq` transports; the proof needs one index type). It is not vacuous: `canonical_ArrowIndex : ObjDecEq C → ArrowIndex C` at `TotalMor C` over Construction/Quotient.v's existing `ObjDecEq` (an earlier revision declared a duplicate `DecObj`; the audit found the twin), the round trip by `Coq.Logic.Eqdep_dec.UIP_dec` (a theorem); the terminal category satisfies all three hypotheses, so they are jointly satisfiable, and no non-trivial in-tree instance is exhibited. **The constructive kernel** `freyd_no_separated_pair : False` consumes one elementary `IsIndexedProduct (fun _ : K => b) P pr` and a boolean separator of the pair (respecting `≈`, true on `f`, false on `g`): the `2^K` arrows `fr_mk phi : a ~> P`, read back by `fr_decode`, make the index surject onto `K → bool`, contradicting the four-line `freyd_cantor_bool` (a named twin of Instance/Fun/Discrete.v's `cantor_bool`, which a Structure/ file cannot require; relocation surfaced) — no axiom, no excluded middle, no decidability, no `Set`. **`freyd_thin : ArrowIndex C → HasIndexedProducts C → DecHom C → Thin C`** (`DecHom C := ∀ x y (u v : x ~> y), (u ≈ v) + (u ≈ v → False)`, a `sum` since `≈` is Type-valued) with `freyd_thin_canonical` and the dual `freyd_thin_dual` (products in `C^op`, `Opposite_Thin`); **the issue's pinned `small_complete_is_thin : ArrowIndex C → Complete C → DecHom C → Thin C`** and `small_cocomplete_is_thin` (Riehl §E.1's "or coproducts", via Construction/Product/Limit.v's `Complete_op_of_Cocomplete`) through the NEW `Complete → IsIndexedProduct` bridge `complete_iprod` (any `d : A → C`, through Structure/Limit/Comparison.v's `DiscreteCat_Functor'` and `discrete_IsIndexedProduct_of_IsLimitCone`; - **Instance/Proset/Order.v**: The order-theoretic development over `Instance/Proset.v` — Seven Sketches §§1.2.2/1.3.1 and Riehl §1.2. `Equivalence_is_PreOrder`/`PreOrder_Symmetric_is_Equivalence` (a preorder is an equivalence minus symmetry, both ways); discrete and codiscrete preorders with codiscrete terminal and discrete initial among preorder structures on a carrier (uniqueness clauses included); `comparable x y := (x ≤ y) + (y ≤ x)` with `TotalOrder` characterized by total comparability and a header note separating comparability from decidability; discrete-preorder comparability (self-comparable, distinct incomparable); `nat` a `TotalOrder` with the reverse order exhibited as `(ℕ,≤)^op`; `(Proset P)^op ≅ Proset (flip P)` in Cat (Riehl §1.2); infimum/supremum named and proved to coincide with the discrete-two-object limit/colimit over an *arbitrary preorder* (totality is needed only for existence, not the identification), two-element order worked, colimit half also restated through `IsAColimit` — stated directly; the general identification lemma belongs to issue #422 (whose suggested module is this same directory), and the header records that these are its binary-shape case, to be consumed rather than restated when #422 lands
- **Structure/Terminal.v**: Terminal and initial objects, and their uniqueness — the bundled `Terminal` class with `one`/`one_unique` and, by the `Initial C := Terminal (C^op)` notation, `Structure/Initial.v`'s `zero`/`zero_unique`; uniqueness up to a *unique* isomorphism in three strengths (`terminal_unique` + `terminal_arrow_unique`, packaged as the single `terminal_unique_up_to_unique_iso : ∃! _ : 1 ≅ 1, True` over `iso_setoid`, with the initial duals), and `zero_object_unique`/`zero_object_unique_initial` joined by the proved `zero_object_unique_compat` (Structure/ZeroObject.v). The object-level predicates `IsTerminalObj`/`IsInitialObj` (`∀ x, Unique (fun _ : x ~> c => True)`) convert both ways with the bundled classes and are what let terminality be used as a *property*: repleteness `Terminal_iso`, the full subcategory `TerminalObjects` with `TerminalObjects_Replete` and singleton hom-sets, and — given an inhabitant — `terminal_sub_contractible`, Riehl's Lemma 1.6.16 in full (`EquivalenceOfCategories (Erase (Sub C TerminalObjects))`; the "empty OR contractible" disjunction is *not* stated, since deciding it is excluded middle for "C has a terminal object" — Construction/Subcategory/Terminal.v). `Terminal_transport`/`Initial_transport` carry either object along an equivalence (Theory/Equivalence/Terminal.v). Riehl Exercise 1.6.i gives `terminal_initial_arrow_iso` and with it `ZeroObject_from_arrow`, the first in-tree construction that *derives* `zero_coincide` rather than assuming it. Terminality as a universal property is `TerminalIsUniversalProperty`/`InitialIsUniversalProperty` — the instance `Structure/UniversalProperty.v`'s `univ_property_unique_up_to_unique_iso` had always lacked at its own illustrating case — with `terminal_unique_up_to_unique_iso_via_UP` re-deriving the concrete statement through it (Structure/UniversalProperty/Terminal.v). Strict initiality is `initial_strict : (x ~> 0) → x ≅ 0` with `initial_strict_unique` (Structure/BiCCC.v — cartesian closed + initial suffices, no `Cocartesian`), instantiated at `Sets` and at skeletal `FinSet`, where it computes to `∀ x : nat, (x ~> 0) → x = 0` (Structure/BiCCC/Strict.v)
- **Structure/Cartesian.v**: Products via universal property
- **Structure/Cartesian/Closed.v**: Exponentials and internal hom (the live
  cartesian-closed development; `Structure/Closed.v` is an incomplete
  Eilenberg–Kelly stub whose `Class Closed` is not yet in force). The currying
  adjunction is packaged in Structure/Cartesian/Closed/Adjunction.v: the
  endofunctors `Prod_Functor S = (− × S)` and `Exp_Functor S = (−)^S` (the
  latter the partial application of Functor/Hom/Internal.v's internal-hom
  bifunctor, `Exp_Functor_InternalHom`), the named naturality lemma
  `eval_natural` with its bundled `eval_Transform : (−)^S × S ⟹ Id`, and
  `Curry_Adjunction : Prod_Functor S ⊣ Exp_Functor S` in the hom-set form of
  Theory/Adjunction.v — `curry`/`uncurry` as the transposes and `eval` as
  counit, all three by `reflexivity`, with the triangle identities inherited
  from the general theory; this turns the prose remark in Theory/Adjunction.v's
  header into a theorem. `Curry_Representable` is the first instance of
  `Functor/Representable.v`'s class (and its first consumer: resolution finds
  it, and the class's `Representable_to_obj` coercion reads the representing
  object back), witnessing Riehl's Example 2.1.6(iv) — the presheaf
  `C(− × S, B) : C^op ⟶ Sets` is represented by `B^S`, with the Yoneda
  universal element `eval` (`Curry_repr_universal`). That is a claim about
  THAT class: representability content also lives under
  `Structure/UniversalProperty.v`'s `IsUniversalProperty`, which has three
  instances. Note also that the counit's being `eval` on the nose is a
  consequence of the transposes alone, not of defining the exponential
  endofunctor directly — what the direct definition buys is that the four
  naturality fields discharge from the `Closed` corollaries verbatim
  (audit-corrected). The `Sets` model, where the counit computes to
  `e(h, s) = h s` and the transpose of addition on a `nat` setoid witnesses
  non-vacuity, is Instance/Sets/Cartesian/Closed/Adjunction.v, which also
  carries the Mac Lane §V.4 corollary that `− × X` preserves all colimits

The proof is in three steps: `wide_empty_id_IsWideEqualizer` (the identity satisfies the record over an empty index), `wide_unpointed_round_trip_gives_hom` (an unpointed round trip landing at that same apex, applied to it, manufactures an arrow `x ~> y` from nothing, by reading the limit leg at `ParY`), and `wide_round_trip_needs_point` (instantiate at `_2` with `x := TwoY`, `y := TwoX`, whose hom-set is empty — `False`). The binary donor never meets this because its `fork_legs h ParY := f ∘ h` silently uses the distinguished member. What needs NO inhabitant, holding at every index including the empty one: `wide_equalizer_monic`/`wide_coequalizer_epic`, `wide_equalizer_unique`/`wide_coequalizer_unique`, `wide_limit_equalizes`/`wide_colimit_coequalizes`. `HasWideEqualizers`/`HasWideCoequalizers` are declared but NOT inhabited for any category. A plain `Definition`, not a `Class`, and never registered for resolution (the Theory/Equivalence.v rule — it carries a *chosen* inverse), with the `ginv` calculus (`ginv_unique_r`/`ginv_unique_l` from `comp_inverse_unique`, `ginv_respects` derived rather than assumed, involution/identity/composite, and `ginv_choice_irrelevant`: any two `IsGroupoid` structures agree up to `≈`). Groups ARE one-object groupoids, as a biconditional: `deloop_groupoid_iff : MonInverses M ↔ IsGroupoid (Deloop M)` (Fong–Spivak §3.2.5 Exercise 3.32), with both witnesses PROVED — `deloop_nat_not_groupoid` exhibits the arrow `1` of `B (ℕ,+)` as non-invertible, `deloop_bool_groupoid` is `B (Z/2)` — and `vertex_group G x : GrpObject` for the converse, round-tripping with `Deloop` on the nose in both data fields. `conjugation_iso G f : MonIso (vertex_group G x) (vertex_group G x')` is Mac Lane's conjugation, over locally defined `MonHom`/`MonIso` (a group homomorphism needs no separate class: `MonHom_grp_inv` derives preservation of inverses). **Structure/Groupoid/Connected.v** adds `ZigZag`/`Connected` in Riehl's §1.5 finite-zig-zag form — with `Fence` (strictly alternating spans) interderivable with it, and `zigzag_hom`/`hom_zigzag` collapsing it to the one-arrow form for groupoids — and the structure theorem `connected_deloop_equiv` (Riehl Proposition 1.5.13): a connected groupoid is equivalent to `B (hom(x,x))` at any object x, through `vertex_incl` (fully faithful with no hypothesis, essentially surjective by connectedness). The hypothesis is proven NECESSARY: `connected_iff_deloop_equiv` is a biconditional, and `Two_Discrete_no_deloop_equivalence` refutes the conclusion for the disconnected 2-object discrete groupoid. Non-vacuity: `WideDeloop M A` (the delooping widened over an object type A) gives the 2-object connected groupoid `Bool_Wide` with vertex group Z/2 at which the theorem is instantiated; `Roof_Connected` + `Roof_not_arrow_connected` prove the zig-zag form STRICTLY weaker than the one-arrow form outside groupoids. **Structure/Groupoid/Inversion.v** is Riehl Example 1.3.14: the identity-on-objects inversion functor and `Inversion_iso : C ≅[StrictCat] C^op` — stated in `StrictCat` because `≅[Cat]` in this library IS equivalence, with `Inversion_Cat_iso` the weaker derived form; the Z/2 instance is flagged degenerate (every element is its own inverse) and `Z3_Grp` is added so `Z3_inversion_not_identity` exhibits the functor actually moving an arrow. **Structure/Groupoid/Basepoint.v** turns the structure theorem into a group isomorphism: `Full_Compose`/`Faithful_Compose`, then `deloop_ff_moniso` — a fully faithful functor between one-object categories IS a monoid isomorphism, the content being that `Full`'s `prefmap` is only a section with no functoriality demanded, so that it is a homomorphism must be proved, and faithfulness is what proves it — and `deloop_equiv_moniso`, `connected_vertex_moniso` (the vertex groups at any two objects of a connected groupoid are isomorphic), instantiated at `Bool_Wide_vertex_moniso`. That instantiation is honest about its own weakness: `WideDeloop` fixes the hom type uniformly (`hom := fun _ _ => carrier M`), so the vertex groups at the two DISTINCT objects are the SAME monoid — `Bool_Wide_vertex_groups_agree` records it by `eq_refl` and `Bool_Wide_vertex_moniso_trivial` inhabits the same type with the identity maps alone — so the witness exercises the two HYPOTHESES and the derivation, not the conclusion; no in-tree object does better (docs/INHABITATION.md carries the note). The longer route is taken deliberately over `conjugation_iso`'s short one; the two words are kept in their exact senses (the structure theorem gives an equivalence of categories, what comes out is a bijection of underlying setoids preserving unit and multiplication). - **Construction/FreeMonoidal.v**: The free monoidal category on one generator — Mac Lane §VII.2 in full (`maclane:VII.2:def1/construction1/thm1`). Binary words `Word` (exported standalone for the §VII.2 coherence corollary and §XI word-functors), the category `W` with hom the length equation and a constantly-true hom-setoid (Instance/Proset.v's thin-category device), so `W_thin` discharges every categorical, bifunctorial and monoidal law uniformly — the file contains no coherence argument, and `wlen`'s structural `+` makes the left unitor literally `eq_refl`. FreeMonoidal/Normal.v is the engine room via the strictification/NbE route (Beylin–Dybjer, Schauenburg; disclosed — the statement is Mac Lane's, the route is not his rank induction): the tail-parameterised `nf`/`J`/`subst`/`can` all typecheck by conversion with no transport in any definition, every cast has the single shape `id_cast (f_equal (nf -) e)` over a nat equality (so cast-UIP is Hedberg, axiom-free, and no `ObjDecEq` on the target is needed), and the two theorems where the target's coherence is spent are `J_assoc` (the pentagon) and `J_right_unit` (triangle + Kelly). FreeMonoidal/Universal.v proves Theorem 1: `Subst` with `Subst_tensor` (Mac Lane's `T(f□g) = Tf□'Tg`), the three strictness equations, `Subst_Monoidal` (strong) and `Subst_Strict` — both object equations `eq_refl` ON THE NOSE, witnessed by Examples — and the uniqueness triad `JW_unique`/`canW_unique`/`Subst_unique` with the package `FreeMonoidal_universal`: object agreement `Theta` is DERIVED from strictness plus the single datum `G WI = b` (where the PROP precedent takes the whole family as a hypothesis), and arrow agreement holds for every arrow by thinness decomposition through the normalisers. The morphism notion is STRICT because that is Mac Lane's: his Moncat has strict morphisms as arrows (`maclane:VII.1:construction2`), and uniqueness among strong monoidal functors is false; uniqueness up to monoidal natural isomorphism needs a class the tree lacks (ledger 19)
- **Construction/Deloop.v**: Delooping — Mac Lane §I.2 constructions 3 and 4, the monoid/one-object-category dictionary. `MonObject` is a bare setoid monoid (carrier + unit + op + `Proper` + the three laws), deliberately NOT `Theory/Algebra/Monoid.v`'s internal monoid object, since the construction needs an *element*-level multiplication and nothing about an ambient monoidal category; it is `Instance/CMon.v`'s `CMonObject` minus commutativity, so it carries both unit laws as fields rather than deriving one. `Deloop M : Category` has `obj := poly_unit` (universe-polymorphic, so the object universe stays free rather than pinned at `Set`) and `hom _ _ := carrier M`, composition the multiplication. The converse is `hom_monoid C a : MonObject`, the endomorphism monoid of any object, and the two compose definitionally: `hom_monoid_Deloop : hom_monoid (Deloop M) ttt = M` holds by `eq_refl`. (The opposite composite has no equational form — `Deloop (hom_monoid C a)` is one-object while `C` need not be — and the honest statement, that it is the full subcategory on `{a}`, is functor-level and deferred with the §I.3 dictionary.) `GrpObject` extends `MonObject` with a two-sided inverse, and `Deloop_group_invertible` makes every arrow of `Deloop G` invertible, with `to` the arrow and `from` the group inverse — a one-object groupoid. (The companion `Deloop_group_iso` has a vacuous *type*, since `obj[Deloop G]` is a singleton; the content is in `Deloop_group_invertible`.) `Construction/Deloop/Opposite.v` adds the opposite monoid and group and Riehl Example 1.2.2(iii), `Deloop_op : (Deloop M)^op ≅ Deloop (MonObject_op M)`. Witnesses `Nat_Plus`, `Bool_Xor`, `Bool_Xor_Grp` compute. Distinct from `Theory/Bicategory/OneObject.v`, which deloops a *monoidal category* into a one-object *bicategory*, one level up

THE BOOKS, from the page images: Mac Lane ends §VI.2 with "several examples which show that the T-algebras for familiar monads are the familiar algebras"; for a group G, TX = G × X with η x = ⟨u, x⟩ and μ⟨g₁, ⟨g₂, x⟩⟩ = ⟨g₁g₂, x⟩ "define a monad ⟨T, η, μ⟩ on Set", and a T-algebra h : G × X → X is one "such that always h(g₁g₂, x) = h(g₁, h(g₂, x)), h(u, x) = x", "the usual conditions that ⟨g, x⟩ ↦ g · x defines an action". The printed action law has the orientation of `MSetoidAction`'s `act_op` (act (g h) x ≈ act g (act h x)); Monad/Algebra.v's `t_action` states t_alg ∘ fmap t_alg ≈ t_alg ∘ join, the two sides exchanged, so the action law of an algebra read as an action is the symmetry of `t_action` (a scouting reading of the PDF's text layer gave the contrary orientation and was discarded; the page image settles it). Riehl, "For any group G": the forgetful functor U : Set^BG → Set has a left adjoint sending X to "the G-set G × X, with G acting on the left", and the exercise asks to "Prove that this adjunction is monadic by appealing to the monadicity theorem", her Theorem 5.5.1, "A right adjoint functor U : D → C is monadic if and only if it creates coequalizers of U-split pairs". **WHICH "MONADIC" IS IMPLEMENTED**: Riehl's — her Definition 5.3.1 calls an adjunction monadic when the comparison functor "defines an equivalence of categories", which is Monad/Comparison.v's `Monadic`, and `beck_monadicity` is the "if" half of her Theorem 5.5.1 in that form. Mac Lane (§VI.3, printed p. 143) says instead that G is monadic when the comparison functor K "will be an isomorphism", and his Beck theorem (§VI.7 Theorem 1, printed p. 151) is stated for that strict form, "creates" meaning a unique lift on the nose; Riehl's p. 202 names the strict reading ("strictly creates") and leaves it to her Exercise 5.5.i. The `≅[Cat]` of both files is the tree's isomorphism in `Cat`, inverse up to natural isomorphism, hence an equivalence; the strict form is NOT delivered (below). **ENCODING DECISIONS, WITH REASONS**. (1) THE CATEGORY OF G-SETS IS REUSED, NOT BUILT: Instance/Fun/Action.v's `MSet M` — the actions `MSetoidAction` of Construction/Deloop/Functors.v with `Equivariant` maps, for any `MonObject` M of Construction/Deloop.v — with `MSet_Fun_equiv : [Deloop M, Sets] ≅[Cat] MSet M`, which identifies it with Riehl's Set^BG; statements are over a monoid because neither the monad nor the algebra correspondence uses inverses; the file sits beside its donor. (2) THE MONAD IS THE MONAD OF AN ADJUNCTION, its laws not proved by hand: `FreeAct X` is M × X acted on in the left factor, g · (h, x) = (g h, x); `MSet_adj : MSet_Free M ⊣ MSet_Forget M` is built on hom-setoids by Theory/Adjunction.v's `Build_Adjunction'` (an equivariant φ out of M × X restricts to x ↦ φ (u, x), `MSet_restrict`, and ψ extends to (g, x) ↦ g · ψ x, `MSet_extend`); `ActF M := MSet_Forget M ◯ MSet_Free M` and `ActMonad M := Adjunction_Induced_Monad (MSet_adj M)` (Monad/Comparison.v), whose `ret` is η and `join` U ε F, both transparent, so Mac Lane's formulas read back at `eq_refl` (`ActF_obj`, `ActF_map`, `ActMonad_ret` at a point and `ActMonad_ret_fun` as a function, `ActMonad_join` at his triple and `ActMonad_join_fun` as a function, the stronger form for μ since Coq's `prod` has no eta) and the laws are those Monad/Comparison.v derives for any adjunction — the pattern of Instance/Grp/FreeAFT.v's `free_group_monad`. A functor built by hand with the same object and arrow maps (the probe's) agrees with `ActF M` in `fobj` and `fmap` at `eq_refl` and as a functor at ≈ only, the proof fields differing, so no second monad is kept. (3) ALGEBRAS ARE ACTIONS: `EM_act` reads an algebra (X, h) as g · x := h (g, x) (unit law `t_id`, action law the symmetry of `t_action`); `EM_to_MSet` is the functor, and with `EM_Comparison` it forms `MSet_comparison_equivalence`, identity components both ways; hence `MSet_Forget_Monadic_direct` and `EM_MSet_iso : MSet M ≅[Cat] EilenbergMoore (ActF M)`, whose `to` leg IS `EM_Comparison (MSet_adj M)` (`EM_MSet_iso_to`), whose `from` leg IS `EM_to_MSet M` (`EM_MSet_iso_from`), and whose comparison algebra is the action, at (g, a) (`comparison_alg_is_action`) and as a function (`comparison_alg_fun`); `Fun_EM_iso` composes `MSet_Fun_equiv` with it, so Set^BG is isomorphic in `Cat` to the algebras. (4) MONADICITY BY BECK, AS RIEHL ASKS, AND DIRECTLY: `MSet_Forget_creates : CreatesUSplitCoequalizers (MSet_Forget M)` in Beck.v's isomorphism-invariant sense — over a split coequalizer e : U B → Z with sections s and t, the created M-set is Z itself with g · z := e (g · s z) (`CreatedAct`), its action law and the equivariance of e both resting on one absorption, a map out of B that coforks the pair absorbing s ∘ e (`split_absorb`, `created_absorb`, the only `Qed` lemmas of the two files). The lift chosen is on the nose — carrier Z, action e (g · s z), arrow e and comparison isomorphism `iso_id` (`mset_created_carrier`, `mset_created_action`, `mset_created_arrow`, `mset_created_iso`) — although the class asks only for an isomorphism; uniqueness of such a lift, Mac Lane's strict creation, is not claimed. `MSet_beck_equivalence := beck_monadicity (MSet_adj M) (MSet_Forget_creates M)` is the tree's FIRST application of `beck_monadicity` (`grep -lw beck_monadicity` over the `.v` files at master 05c9bf73 lists Beck.v alone), with `MSet_Forget_Monadic` from it and `MSet_Forget_reflects` (a bijective equivariant map is an isomorphism) as Beck.v's `creates_split_reflects_isos` at this instance. The two routes are equivalences OF THE SAME FUNCTOR, on the nose: the `to` leg of `EM_MSet_iso_beck` (Beck's equivalence through `Equivalence_to_Cat_Iso`) IS `EM_Comparison (MSet_adj M)` (`EM_MSet_iso_beck_to`) and equals the direct route's (`beck_direct_to`); their quasi-inverses differ — Beck's keeps the carrier (`beck_carrier`) and acts through η, g · z = h (g u, z) (`beck_act`, Monad/Monadicity/BeckObjects.v's `canonical_split` having `ret` as its section), and is ≈ to `EM_to_MSet` with identity components (`beck_vs_direct`). The crude route of Monad/Monadicity/Crude.v was not taken: it needs `HasReflexiveCoequalizers (MSet M)`, quotient setoids stable under the action, and the preservation of every reflexive coequalizer upstairs, where the precise route needs no quotient (reasoned, not compiled). (5) RIEHL'S LITERAL Set^BG (BG.v), since no lemma in the tree transports `Monadic` along an equivalence such as `MSet_Fun_equiv` (a grep): `SetBG M` is `[Deloop M, Sets]` with its hom level written out, `U_BG M` Instance/Fun/Eval.v's `Eval` at the one object `ttt` and `F_BG M := MSet_from M ◯ MSet_Free M`; evaluation agrees with `MSet_Forget ◯ MSet_to` in both data fields at `eq_refl` (`U_BG_obj`, `U_BG_map`) and not as a functor; `BG_adj : F_BG M ⊣ U_BG M` is built by `Build_Adjunction'`, `BG_extend` reusing `MSet_extend` through Instance/Fun/Action.v's `MSet_round_iso`. CREATION BY TRANSPORT: a split coequalizer of the `U_BG`-images of p, q IS, by conversion, one of the `MSet_Forget`-images of `MSet_to p` and `MSet_to q` (`action_of_functor P` has carrier P ttt and action fmap[P]), so Monad.v's `CreatedAct`, `CreatedE` (whose equivariance is `BGCreatedE`'s naturality), `CreatedE_is_coeq` (through Beck.v's `coequalizer_along_iso` at `MSet_action_round_iso`) and `Reflected_is_coeq` are used as they stand, the one new lemma being `MSet_to_reflects_coeq` (a cofork of transformations whose `MSet_to`-image is a coequalizer of M-sets is a coequalizer of functors); measured in non-whitespace characters with comments excluded, `U_BG_creates` and its three new constants take 2541 against 6385 for the scouting prototype that re-proved the creation at the functor category. That lift is on the nose too (`bg_created_carrier`, `bg_created_action`, `bg_created_arrow`, `bg_created_iso`). `BG_beck_equivalence := beck_monadicity (BG_adj M) (U_BG_creates M)` is the second application, with `U_BG_Monadic`, `U_BG_reflects` (a transformation whose component at the one object is invertible in `Sets` is invertible), `BGMonad M := Adjunction_Induced_Monad (BG_adj M)` and `BG_EM_iso`, whose `to` leg IS `EM_Comparison (BG_adj M)` (`BG_EM_iso_to`). THE TWO INDUCED MONADS DIFFER AT THE UNIT: `BGMonad`'s functor has `ActF`'s object and arrow maps (`BG_T_obj`, `BG_T_map`), its multiplication is Mac Lane's at his triple and as a function (`BG_join`, `BG_join_fun`) and agrees with `ActMonad`'s at every argument (`BG_join_ActMonad`), the two differing as setoid morphisms only in their properness proofs; but its unit is x ↦ (u u, x) at `eq_refl` (`BG_ret`, and as a function `BG_ret_fun`), Mac Lane's printed (u, x) being refused: the unit is the restriction of the identity of F X, and the identity of the functor category is Theory/Natural/Transformation.v's `nat_id`, whose component is fmap[F X] id, the action of u. The functors are ≈ with identity components (`BG_T_ActF`) and the units ≈ by `mon_op_unit_l` (`BG_ret_ActMonad`). Universal property in Karoubi/Universal.v: `IdempotentsSplit` (chosen splittings, satisfied by every envelope), `Karoubi_Extend` along the embedding with `Extend ∘ Embed ≈ G` and uniqueness up to `≈`, `CauchyComplete := IdempotentsSplit`, and split idempotents ⇒ the embedding is an equivalence (forward direction); Sets is Cauchy complete (Instance/Sets/Karoubi.v via the fixed-point sub-setoid)

- **Instance/Ab.v**: `Ab`, the category of abelian groups (Mac Lane §I.7) — `AbObject` extends `Instance/CMon.v`'s `CMonObject` by a negation (`ab_cmon :> CMonObject`), so carrier and the four monoid laws are inherited; `AbHom` IS `CMonHom`, making preservation of negation the theorem `ab_map_neg` rather than a field. `Ab_Forget : Ab ⟶ Sets`; `Ab_Zero` from the one-element group. Mac Lane's §I.7 proposition in both halves: `ab_monic_iff_injective` probing with `AbKernel`, and `ab_epic_iff_surjective` probing with the quotient `AbQuotient` = B/fA — the epic half now concluding the PROPOSITIONAL surjectivity `AbPropSurjective`, an earlier revision of this bullet having stated it against the Σ-valued `AbSurjective`: measured on 2026-09-17 after the PR "algebraic carriers are sets", `ab_coset_eq` is `Prop`-valued (an `ex` over the carrier's `pequiv`, `Instance/Ab.v`), so `ab_epic_surjective` and the biconditional conclude the truncated notion, while `AbSurjective`, `ab_surjective_epic` and the Σ→`Epic` half are byte-identical to their pre-PR statements — in a category of sets epi implies surjective, and surjective implies SPLIT only with choice. The quotient probe is available here for ONE reason — commutativity: `ab_coset_eq` is a congruence only because `f a` can be commuted past another element (`cmon_plus_comm` in `AbQuotient`'s `cmon_plus_respects`), which is what makes B/fA an OBJECT of `Ab` rather than a bare setoid. No comparative claim is made against `Sets`: `Instance/Sets.v` now proves `surjectivity_is_epic` outright via a cokernel-pair setoid — the same kind of quotient probe — so both categories have the result and both get it the same way. NOTE the monic half is NOT special to `Ab` — monic ⟹ injective already holds in `CMon`, probing with `nat`; the kernel is a convenient probe, not a necessary one. SCOPE: `Preadditive Ab` and a forgetful `Ab ⟶ Grp` are NOT delivered, and this file instantiates none of `Preadditive`/`Additive`/`Abelian`. What it does NOT show is that #330's suggested `Proset` route is impossible: the argument covered only SQUASHING a Type-valued hom, never making MEMBERSHIP itself Prop-valued, and under that variant `FGHom` is natively a `relation`, nothing is squashed, `fmap` merely applies a `Prop → Prop` function into a `sigT`, and the colimit goes through (audit-built, closed under the global context; the transport and the `Proset` application independently re-checked).
