- **Instance/Variety/Free.v**: Mac Lane §V.6 (book p. 124) — **the free-algebra adjunction for a variety, and it is AXIOM-FREE**. **AN EARLIER REVISION OF THIS BULLET JUSTIFIED THE DESIGN WITH A CLAIM THAT IS FALSE**, and the correction is the most useful thing here. It said the free object CANNOT live in #440's Leibniz `Variety E` because Coq has no quotient types. Refuted by construction: the free commutative magma on two generators DOES exist there, built by sorting terms into normal forms under a decidable total order, with its universal arrow packaged through the same `universal_arrow_from_UMP` this file uses; and a cheap in-tree witness of the same point, `free_empty_eq_leibniz`, shows that with no equations the term algebra is already a Leibniz-variety object. What IS true is two-part. (i) The TERM ALGEBRA is not a Leibniz-variety object once the equations bite — `free_magma_not_comm_leibniz` proves `x*y` and `y*x` are different terms, via a leftmost-generator measure so the refutation needs no projection out of `node`'s dependent argument (an earlier revision justified that measure by an `Eqdep` risk in the injection route, which is also false HERE, since both sides carry the same literal operation — the measure is kept because it stays robust when they do not). (ii) Making it land requires a computable NORMAL FORM per presentation, i.e. solving that presentation's word problem, which is not available uniformly. **So the setoid carrier buys UNIFORMITY in ⟨Ω,E⟩, not existence** — `Free_Variety` is defined for every `E` with no decidability hypothesis. The setoid variety sits beside the Leibniz one in deliberately the same `Sub` shape (`SetoidAlgs`, `ssatisfies`, `SVariety`); `SVariety_Forget` carries the algebra's own setoid where #440's lands on the discrete one, and that too buys uniformity rather than existence (an earlier revision said it was "what lets a free object exist over it"). **The congruence is axiom-free, and #440's header said it could not be**: `tree_equiv` takes symmetry and transitivity as CONSTRUCTORS rather than theorems, so no inversion is ever performed and the `Eqdep`/`JMeq_eq` hazard that `Instance/Variety/Clone.v` feared does not arise; `tc_refl` is derived by plain induction, and that file's not-delivered block is corrected in place to say so. An earlier revision said here "It must be `Type`-valued, since `Setoid`'s `equiv` is a crelation"; since #450 it is `Prop`-valued (`About tree_equiv` ends in `→ Prop`, and `tree_equiv_rect`/`tree_equiv_rec` no longer exist) — the crelation field accepts a `Prop` relation by cumulativity, and `free_alg_ext_respects` now goes through the target's `pequiv_to` — which is what makes the congruence indexes of `Instance/Variety/Colimit.v` carrier-sized. **THE HEADLINE MEASUREMENT**: `Free_Variety_adjunction : Free_Variety_Functor E ⊣ SVariety_Forget E` is **Closed under the global context**, as is the whole general theory — and #440's `GroupVariety` is not. The two are consistent and the reason is exact: the equations enter here ONLY through `EqSignature`'s `lhs_natural`/`rhs_natural` (an earlier revision said "consumed in one place, `free_alg_ext_respects`'s `tc_law` case", already false then — `soa_prod_satisfies` consumes them too — and since #450 `Instance/Variety/Limit.v`'s `svlim_satisfies` and `Instance/Variety/Colimit.v`'s `vker_cong` also do), and every construction CONSUMES those fields, so #440's `functional_extensionality_dep` is the price of BUILDING an `EqSignature`, not of using one. Exactly four constants carry the axiom, all by instantiating at `GroupEq` or by construction — `SGroupVariety`, `FreeGroupOn`, `FreeGroup_adjunction`, `leibniz_soa` — and they are not gated. The adjunction is packaged through `universal_arrow_from_UMP` and `AdjunctionFromUniversalArrows`, the same two steps `Construction/Free/Quiver.v` uses; **GAFT was considered and loses on four counts**, of which the `Set` universe pin is the LEAST — it would need `Complete (SVariety E)`, `PreservesImageLimit` for the forgetful functor, and a `SolutionSet` with §V.7's cardinality bound, which does not exist constructively here at all because `Instance/Comp.v` makes arities ARBITRARY TYPES rather than finite ones. **CORRECTION (#450): none of the four counts stands** — `Instance/Variety/Limit.v` supplies `SVariety_Complete` and `SVariety_Forget_continuous`, a solution set needs a carrier-universe index rather than a cardinality bound (`Instance/Variety/Colimit.v`'s `SVariety_Forget_solution_set`, the `Prop`-valued congruences on the term algebra), and the `Set` pin went with the PR "algebraic carriers are sets", so `Free_Variety_via_GAFT` is Mac Lane's own route and `Free_Variety_via_GAFT_agrees` identifies it with `Free_Variety_Functor` up to natural isomorphism; the direct construction stays primary because `GAFT` is `Qed`, which leaves no `eq_refl` readback such as `p441_left_adjoint_obj`. **Fields are not a variety** (`fields_are_not_a_variety`), and the proof is NOT the issue's stated motivation that inversion is partial: it is Mac Lane's own, that varieties are closed under products and fields are not, via `soa_prod_satisfies` and `F2 × F2`. That theorem ships in TWO strengths for a reason an audit exposed: a first revision proved it of a predicate imposing only the DIVISION property — no ring axioms, no `1 ≉ 0` — which the one-element algebra and a unit-less "ring" both satisfy, so no `E` whose models are exactly the fields could satisfy that theorem's soundness hypothesis and the theorem said nothing about such an `E`. That weaker statement now ships under the name it deserves, `division_is_not_equationally_definable`, and `fields_are_not_a_variety` is restated over an `IsField` carrying the ring axioms, additive inverses (a Σ-clause, since `RingOp` has no negation), `1 ≉ 0` and division. Since #450 the setoid algebras carry `soa_prop`, so `soa_prod_satisfies` ranges over propositional algebras only, `not_equationally_definable` is incomparable with its earlier form, and the two non-examples, whose witness `F2` is propositional, are weakly STRONGER (Free.v's section "The carrier's `≈` is a proposition (#450)"). `soa_prod` is the componentwise construction only — two projections, no pairing map, no uniqueness — so it is NOT established to be the categorical product, and the name is descriptive; closure under it is all the non-example needs. Measured: 71 `.glob` heads plus 22 `Program` obligations, of which **89 are Closed under the global context and all 89 are gated** (7456 → 7545, axiom audit passing; since #450 the gate names 91 constants of this file, `soa_prop` and `Build_SetoidOpAlgebra` added, all closed, by `grep -o 'Print Assumptions Category\.Instance\.Variety\.Free\.[A-Za-z0-9_]*' Makefile | sort -u | wc -l`, 89 at the parent); four `Defined`, exactly ONE load-bearing (`FreeUA`, whose flip to `Qed` stops the probe's `p441_left_adjoint_obj` readback). NOT delivered: no `Free_Variety : Variety E` — and note the corrected reason, that it exists whenever the presentation has a computable normal form but not uniformly, the 250-line normal-form construction for the one presentation not being shipped; no functor `Variety E ⟶ SVariety E`, `leibniz_soa` being an object map only; no general non-collapse statement, the free algebra being legitimately a single `≈`-class for an `E` whose laws identify everything; no Birkhoff HSP theorem — the non-example is stated over a FIXED signature and rules out every `EqSignature RingOp` whose models are exactly the fields, no more; no cardinality bound (an earlier revision continued "and so no GAFT route"; since #450 the route exists without the bound, above); and no free ring, free abelian group or free module as named instances, the two shipped instances being the ones the issue's own Verification block runs
- **Instance/Matr.v**: Mac Lane §I.2's matrix category, stated over a RIG per the issue's QA corrections (the category laws never subtract): `Matr (R : RigObject)` with objects the naturals and an arrow `n ~> m` an m × n matrix `Fin.t m → Fin.t n → carrier R` (Mac Lane's orientation, documented), composition the matrix product, identity the Kronecker `delta` (spending `Fin.eq_dec`), morphism equality entrywise. The engine is a reusable rig-parameterized finite-sum library — `fin_sum` with congruence, additivity, exchange (`fin_sum_swap`) spending only the additive half (`rig_cmon`; a monoid-level refounding is disclosed-deferred), bilinearity (`fin_sum_mul_l/r`, where distributivity and annihilation are spent), and the Kronecker collapses (`fin_sum_delta_l/r`) — kept general for the GL_n/determinant issue. `Matr_N := Matr Nat_Rig` is Awodey §1.4's category of ℕ-matrices with computing `eq_refl` examples. The transpose self-duality (Mac Lane §II.3 Ex 4, Riehl 1.3.14(v)): for a COMMUTATIVE rig — exactly where (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ spends commutation — `Matr_Transpose` is an identity-on-objects functor to the opposite, involutive on the nose, packaged as the isomorphism of categories `Matr_transpose_iso : Matr R ≅[Cat] (Matr R)^op`, instantiated at ℕ (`Matr_N_transpose_iso`) and at Mac Lane's own commutative-ring headline ℤ (`Matr_Z`, `Matr_Z_transpose_iso`), with the one-element-rig collapse sanity (`Matr_zero_collapse`); over a non-commutative rig the transpose lands in matrices over the opposite rig, noted and deferred. Instance/Matr/Yoneda.v is Riehl Corollary 2.2.10 made categorical: a row operation IS a natural endomorphism of the represented presheaf `[Hom ─,n]` (naturality = commuting with right multiplication, both directions stated), and `row_operations_are_left_multiplication` derives — purely from `Yoneda_Embedding`'s round trips, no entry ever inspected — that every row operation is left multiplication by the unique matrix obtained by applying it to the identity (`representing_matrix_at_id`, `representing_matrix_unique`), with the two-row swap as the computing witness (its representing matrix is the permutation matrix by `eq_refl` over ℕ)
- **Instance/Matr/Elimination.v**, **Instance/Matr/Coequalizer.v**: Mac Lane §III.3 Exercise 3 — coequalizers in the matrix category, delivered at FULL strength: **`Matr_HasCoequalizers`** inhabits `HasCoequalizers (Matr K)` for EVERY parallel pair over ANY field with a zero decider, built on a genuine Gaussian-elimination engine rather than an interface. `Instance/Matr/Elimination.v` is that engine: `LeftNullBasis` (`lnb_dim`/`lnb_basis`/`lnb_annih`/`lnb_univ`) with `left_null_basis` inhabited for every matrix, by recursion on COLUMNS (pivot search, then the basis `e_{d r} − (c_{d r}/c_p)·e_p` indexed through `Determinant.v`'s `fin_delete`), plus the pre-shaped `left_null_basis_diff` and the subtraction kit `mat_sub`/`mat_mul_sub_r`/`mat_sub_zero`/`mat_mul_sub_zero_iff`. **THE DECIDABILITY HYPOTHESIS IS FORCED RATHER THAN CHOSEN — argued, not proved**: `FieldObject` (Instance/FdVect.v) carries NO decider — `finv` is TOTAL and `finv_l` is GUARDED by `x ≉ 0` — and elimination must DECIDE whether a pivot is zero, so a zero-decider is carried as explicit data on the `Instance/Field.v` `field_dec_stable` precedent. Correspondingly **a rig will not do**: `Matr R` is over a `RigObject`, which has no subtraction, so the cokernel-of-a-difference framing needs the RING layer's `ring_neg` and nothing here applies to `Matr_N`. **The `Qed`/`Defined` distinction is load-bearing twice over, and both were found by REFUTED probes rather than anticipated.** `Instance/Field.v`'s `F2_Field_dec` and `Q_Field_dec` are `Qed` lemmas: they inhabit the hypothesis perfectly and the engine is total and correct when fed them, but nothing REDUCES through an opaque constant, so the coequalizer object does not compute — transparent copies (`f2_dec`, `q_dec`) are used for every `eq_refl` witness, and `Instance/Field.v` is deliberately NOT modified. Dually, keeping `matr_coeq_desc` a transparent `Definition` rather than a `Qed` lemma is what keeps **the MEDIATOR computing** (`unique_obj (coeq_desc …) F1 F1 = true` by `eq_refl`). The stage handoff is by PURE CONVERSION — all twelve section constants of Coequalizer.v are `:=` bodies with no tactic, no `change` and no transport, consuming `Matr K`'s own `∘` and `≈[Matr K]`; the only friction was imports, `Structure/Coequalizer.v` not re-exporting `Coequalizer`/`APair`/`^op`. Orientation pinned by `eq_refl` (`matrix_is_hom`, `mat_mul_is_compose` with object order (c,b,a), `mat_id_is_id`, `mat_equiv_is_homset_equiv`) — and read the `#[local] Instance Matrix_Setoid` correctly: an earlier draft of this bullet said that last Example NEEDS it, which an audit REFUTED by experiment. The two setoids are CONVERTIBLE, so the Examples close by `eq_refl` either way and deleting the instance outright leaves the file compiling; what it buys is that the two `≈`s are the same TERM rather than merely convertible ones. **Non-vacuity is proved four ways, not asserted**: over F₂ with `A = (1,0)ᵀ`, `B = (0,1)ᵀ` the object is `k = 1` at `m = 2` — neither 0 nor m — with `coeq_f2_obj_not_zero`/`_not_two` by `discriminate` off the computation, `coeq_f2_pair_distinct`, and the sharpest, `coeq_f2_map_not_monic` paired with `coeq_f2_map_epic`: the coequalizing map identifies two provably inequivalent arrows, so it is a PROPER QUOTIENT and not an isomorphism in disguise. A second non-degenerate point `k = 2` at `m = 3`, degenerate controls at `k = m` and `k = 0`, and a ℚ witness where `finv` actually divides (`E = (−2, 1)`). Also `matr_coeq_epic`, `matr_coeq_iso`, `matr_coeq_colimit`, and `Matr_op_HasEqualizers` reading the result through #326's `IsEqualizer_op_of_IsCoequalizer`. - **Instance/Mod/Free.v**: Mac Lane §III.1 construction 1 + §IV.1 construction 1 + Riehl §4.0 — the free module on a setoid, its universal arrow, and the free ⊣ forgetful ADJUNCTION, with `Instance/Vect/Free.v` the vector-space reading. **The issue's own sketch could not be followed and the header argues why, with the obstruction located exactly**: it asks for finitely supported K-valued functions, and the CARRIER is not the problem — a `≈`-respecting function paired with a list witnessing its support is writable over a bare setoid with no decider. The BASIS INSERTION is: the basis vector at `x` is "1 at x, 0 elsewhere", which cannot be WRITTEN without a decider for `x ≈ y`. That is fatal rather than merely restrictive because `RMod_Forget` lands in `Sets`, so the left adjoint must exist for EVERY setoid, decidable or not — a construction available only at decidable setoids yields no adjunction at all. So encoding 1 is not a trade-off, it is unavailable. The carrier is instead an inductive of formal expressions (`fv_gen`/`fv_zero`/`fv_plus`/`fv_neg`/`fv_smul`) with `fv_eq` an inductive congruence closing under exactly the four abelian-group and four module laws plus saturation under X's `≈` and R's `≈` (Instance/Ab/Tensor.v's shape, reflexivity derived; `fv_Setoid` deliberately NOT an instance, that file's convention). **The list description survives as a THEOREM rather than as the carrier** — `fv_normal_form`: every element is `fv_eq` to a finite formal combination `fv_lc l` — so reordering and collection of like terms are consequences of the congruence rather than obligations on the representation. What that buys, measured: every module law is a constructor, so `FreeModObject` is a record literal with ZERO proof obligations — RE-MEASURED on 2026-09-17 after the PR "algebraic carriers are sets" and STILL TRUE (`grep -c '_obligation_' Instance/Mod/Free.glob` returns 0), although the literal gained one field, `cmon_prop := @PropEquiv_of_relation _ fv_Setoid fv_eq …`, which is neither a law nor a constructor and costs no obligation, `fv_eq` having become a `Prop` inductive in that PR; the setoid constraint `x ≈ y ⟹ e_x = e_y` is the constructor `fe_gen`, making respectfulness of the insertion a one-term proof; and the mediator is a `Fixpoint`, so all three homomorphism laws of the linear extension close by `reflexivity` (recorded as `eq_refl` Examples so the claim is machine-checked rather than inferred from which tactic branch fired). What it costs: seven inductions, of which two carry the universal property (`fv_eval_respects`, 14 cases — eight met by a law of the target module, the other six being generator saturation, congruence and the target setoid's symmetry/transitivity — and `fv_extend_unique`, one case per former) while four more exist only to prove `fv_normal_form`; and **coefficient uniqueness is given up** — hence no decision procedure, no dimension, and NO bridge to Instance/FdVect.v's `FdVectObject`, so it is NOT proved here that the free vector space on a finite generating setoid is finite-dimensional in that file's sense. `free_module_adjunction : FreeMod ⊣ RMod_Forget R` and `free_vect_adjunction : FreeVect F ⊣ Vct_Forget F` are the headline artifacts (via `universal_arrow_from_UMP` → `LeftAdjointFunctorFromUniversalArrows` → `AdjunctionFromUniversalArrows`), with §IV.1's TWO naturality clauses stated and proved in the free module's OWN vocabulary — `free_module_naturality_in_set` (by evaluating at a generator) and `_in_module` (pointwise `reflexivity`) — and then `free_module_naturality_in_set_is_to_adj_nat_l` and its sibling recording by `eq_refl` that those statements ARE the class's fields, a Leibniz equality of statements rather than a parallel restatement. The unit computes (`free_module_unit_is_insert`, `_is_generator`) and the forward transpose IS `fv_transpose` (`free_module_transpose_is_adj`), all `eq_refl`; the COUNIT does not, routing through the `Qed`-opaque `ump_universal_arrows`, and `fmap[FreeMod] u` on a generator is `≈` only since `LeftAdjointFunctorFromUniversalArrows` defines `fmap` by factorization — both pinned as `Fail` probes. **Vect/Free.v specializes by CONVERSION, not by transport**: `Vct_F F = RMod (field_ring F)` by `eq_refl` (it is a `Definition`), every vector-space statement inhabited by its `RMod`-level term, and the field layer buys EXACTLY ONE thing — `field_one_neq_zero` is a field of `FieldObject`, so `1 ≉ 0` is discharged for free; nothing else spends `finv` or commutativity, and an earlier header sentence claiming otherwise was corrected. Non-vacuity at THREE prices, each proved and witnessed over ℤ and ℚ: `free_module_scalars_faithful` needs NO hypothesis, `free_module_two_independent` (the basis is linearly independent — the §III.1 statement a reader wants) needs the decider ONLY, and the reason it can drop `1 ≉ 0` is precisely that over the zero ring every scalar is already 0, so it degenerates there to a truth rather than to a falsehood and survives unassisted, its content carried entirely by the nondegenerate case; `free_module_basis_injective` — which IS false over the zero ring — needs decider AND `1 ≉ 0`. That both hypotheses are unavoidable is ARGUED in the section header, not proved: no converse is machine-checked, and the tree's precedent for exactly that claim shape (`arrow_mul_respects_forces_UIP` and siblings) is deliberately not followed CORRECTION (#472): the COUNIT's opacity, and that of `fmap[FreeMod] u`, have two causes, `ump_universal_arrows` and the file's own `free_module_universal`, measured by turning each `Defined` in rebuilt copies (Free.v's header, CORRECTION (#472); issue #1353 tracks the shared lemma); the same adjunction in hom-set form, `free_module_adjunction_hom` (with `free_module_hom_iso`, `fv_eval_pointwise` and three `eq_refl` readbacks), whose counit IS the fold at `eq_refl`, now sits beside it for #472's free R-module monad. Example 5.1.5(i) (printed p. 185, PDF p. 205; `riehl:5.1:example5`) with her Corollary 4.6.3 (printed p. 167), all read from the page images, issue #466 — **the covariant power set of #227 with the singleton unit and the union multiplication is a monad on `Sets`, `Powerset_Monad`, whose functor and unit ARE #227's `Powerset_Prop` and `Powerset_Prop_Singleton` at `eq_refl`; every algebra of it is a complete (join-)semilattice under x ≤ y iff h{x, y} ≈ y with sup S = h S, every complete semilattice is an algebra in that way, and the category `SupLat` of complete semilattices and sup-preserving maps is isomorphic in `Cat` to the Eilenberg–Moore category (`SupLat_EM_iso`), both legs the two functors at `eq_refl` and every component of both natural isomorphisms the identity; beyond the exercise, the free/forgetful adjunction behind the monad and the monadicity of the forgetful functor, the measurement that the monad of that adjunction is NOT literally `Powerset_Monad`, the witnesses P X and Prop = P 1, the theorem that a complete semilattice with a decidable ≈ and two distinct comparable points yields informative weak excluded middle, with its converse at the chain false < true on `bool`, and Riehl's route to the naturality of μ through the direct image as a left adjoint**. THE BOOKS, from the page images: Mac Lane, "Recall that a complete semi-lattice is a partial order Q in which every subset S ⊂ Q has a supremum (least upper bound) in Q", with 𝒫 the covariant power set, (𝒫f)S the direct image, η_X x = {x} and μ_X the union: "(a) Prove that ⟨𝒫, η, μ⟩ is a monad 𝒫 on Set. (b) Prove that each 𝒫-algebra ⟨X, h⟩ is a complete semi-lattice when x ≦ y is defined by h{x, y} = y, and sup S = hS for each S ⊂ X. (c) Prove conversely that every (small) complete semi-lattice is a 𝒫-algebra in this way. (d) Conclude that the category of 𝒫-algebras is the category of all (small) complete semi-lattices, with morphisms the order and sup-preserving functions." Awodey's Example 10.5 sends f to "the image mapping im(f)" with η_X(x) = {x} and μ_X(α) = ⋃α, leaves the naturality and the laws to the reader, and remarks that "monads can, and often do, arise without coming from evident adjunctions"; his Exercise 10.6.5 is that verification. Riehl lists the monad under "Monads also arise in nature" and says that the naturality of the multiplication "makes use of Corollary 4.6.3; the direct image function, as a left adjoint, preserves unions". Mac Lane's order is the JOIN order (h{x, y} is the least upper bound of x and y), so these are nLab's suplattices, the bottom is sup ∅, and nothing mentions meets. **WHICH CONSTANT IS WHICH PART**: (a) is Monad.v's `Powerset_Monad`, assembled by Theory/Monad.v's `Build_Monad` from the union `Powerset_union` and four pointwise lemmas, `Powerset_union_assoc` (μ ∘ Pμ ≈ μ ∘ μP), `Powerset_union_image_singleton` (μ ∘ Pη ≈ id), `Powerset_union_singleton` (μ ∘ ηP ≈ id) and `Powerset_union_natural` (μ natural, proved directly by opening the squashed direct image), η's naturality being #227's own `naturality_sym` field; Awodey's Example 10.5 and Exercise 10.6.5 are exactly (a), and `Powerset_Monad_statement` inhabits the type `Powerset_Prop_Monad_statement` that #227 entered to show the monad statable. (b) is SupLat.v's `TAlgebra_SupLat`: the order is `talg_le`, the Prop squash of h{x, y} ≈ y, with `talg_le_iff` its reading as Mac Lane's condition, and the sup IS h (`EM_to_SupLat_sup`); the functor is `EM_to_SupLat`. (c) is `SupLat_TAlgebra`: the structure map IS the sup (`SupLat_to_EM_alg`), and "in this way" is `sl_sup_pair_le`, x ≤ y iff sup {x, y} ≈ y, so that (b) after (c) gives back the order (`sl_talg_le_iff`); the functor is `SupLat_to_EM`. (d) is `SupLat_EM_equivalence` and `SupLat_EM_iso : SupLat ≅[Cat] EilenbergMoore Powerset_Prop`. A morphism `SupLatHom` is a setoid map preserving sups (`slh_sup`); Mac Lane's "order and sup-preserving" asks for monotonicity too, which is derived (`SupLatHom_monotone`, through `sl_sup_pair_le`), so the two classes of maps are one. Riehl's Example 5.1.5(i) is (a) together with Riehl.v's two routes to μ's naturality (below). **ENCODING DECISIONS, WITH REASONS**. (1) #227 IS REUSED, per the issue's QA correction: the functor `Powerset_Prop` (≈-respecting `Prop`-valued predicates under pointwise ↔, the direct image with its existential squashed) and the unit `Powerset_Prop_Singleton` are used verbatim, η being that transformation's component (`Powerset_Monad_ret`, `Powerset_Monad_ret_map`, `Powerset_Monad_ret_member`, `eq_refl`); the new union ⋃ SS := λ x, ∃ S, SS S ∧ S x needs no squash, both memberships being `Prop`s, and P(P X) stays at X's level by the impredicativity of `Prop` (`Powerset_Monad_join`, `Powerset_Monad_join_at`, `eq_refl`). #227's proof-relevant carrier `Powerset` lands one universe up and carries no monad at all (refused on universes, pinned). Instance/Sets/Powerset.v's code is not edited: the monad is a satellite beside it, the file being imported by 43 `.v` files outside `doc/` at the base commit 0738c74f, 19 of them under `Test/` (a scan of their `Require` commands). (2) THE RECORD IS MAC LANE'S DEFINITION, ORDER FIRST: `SupLatObject` has a setoid `sl_set`, an order `sl_le : carrier → carrier → Prop` of its own, reflexive, transitive, respecting ≈ and antisymmetric into ≈, and a supremum `sl_sup` for every subset, a setoid map out of #227's subsets with `sl_sup_ub` and `sl_sup_least`; `SupLat@{o so} : Category@{so o o}` sits at `Sets@{o so}`'s universes, two morphisms equal when their maps agree pointwise up to ≈. Not the standard library's `relation` with Instance/Proset/Limit.v's `IsLUB` or `HasAllJoins` over it: a record so built carries the global cap o <= Relation_Definition.u0 and two or four extra universe binders (`About` on the scouts' two such records, re-measured in this tree by the first builder and its reviewer). The order is a `Prop` because #227's singletons are: the unit law needs sup {x} ≤ x from a squashed membership, and with a `Type`-valued order that elimination is refused on universes, a sort refusal (pinned: "Cannot enforce o <= Prop"). The sup is a setoid map, not a bare function: with a bare function the round trip rebuilds its respect for ≈ and the structure map comes back only as a function (the rebuilt map refused at `eq_refl`, its function accepted, both in the probe). - **Instance/Discrete.v**: Discrete categories, and Mac Lane §I.2's "a discrete category is determined by its set of objects" — `DiscreteCat A` (objects `A`, morphisms equality proofs) with `DiscreteCat_Discrete` one way, and the reconstruction the other in Instance/Discrete/Reconstruct.v: `Discrete_iso : Discrete C → DiscreteRigid C → C ≅[StrictCat] DiscreteCat obj[C]`, with the `Cat` reading alongside. `DiscreteRigid` is the extra hypothesis and it is stated INTRINSICALLY — the comparison functor is faithful (`DiscreteRigid_Faithful`) — with UIP on objects and decidable object equality as sufficient conditions (`DiscreteRigid_UIP`, `DiscreteRigid_dec`, the latter by Hedberg, axiom-free). It is not an artifact of the proof: `DiscreteCat`'s homset is strict `eq` on equality proofs, so a functor into it must identify parallel proofs. The file also addresses `Structure/Discrete.v`'s long-standing "Equality is too much here" caveat with the iso-robust `DiscreteUpToIso` (subsingleton homs, all arrows invertible), and then shows the two notions are genuinely independent rather than merely differently phrased: `Discrete_DiscreteUpToIso_forces_UIP` proves that `∀ C, Discrete C → DiscreteUpToIso C` would entail UIP for *every* type, and `Indiscrete_bool_Discrete_absurd` with `Indiscrete_DiscreteUpToIso` exhibits a category that is discrete-up-to-iso but not `Discrete`. Functor categories OVER discrete shapes are Instance/Fun/Discrete.v (Mac Lane §II.4): transformations over a discrete domain are bare families with naturality free (`Discrete_Transform`, with the hom-setoid isomorphism `Discrete_hom_iso : (F ⟹ G) ≅[Sets] (∀ a, F a ~> G a)`), `[DiscreteCat A, B] ≅[Cat] PiCat (fun _ => B)` for ANY index type, the finite power `Fun_Discrete_power : [DiscreteCat (Fin.t n), B] ≅ Pow B n` by Fin-peeling entirely at PiCat level (`Pow` carries a trailing terminal factor as its nullary case — n B-factors ∏ `1` — with the literal `B ∏ B` shape exhibited at n = 2 via `prod_one_r`), the power-set computation `Fun_Discrete_bool_subsets` (functors into `DiscreteCat bool` up to natural iso = characteristic functions `X → bool`, the constructive decidable-subsets reading), the axiom-free Cantor diagonal `cantor_predicates`/`cantor_bool` with `Fun_Discrete_no_surjection` connecting it to the correspondence — the size half of Mac Lane's remark, with the universe-sized half rendered structurally by the library's universe discipline — and Seven Sketches 3.53's morphism half `One_hom_iso` (hom-setoid iso in Sets, any target, instantiated at Sets; the object half `[1, C] ≅ C` is Theory/Shapes.v's `One_Fun_iso`, cited not rebuilt)

Reading the block alone reports "no identification" and is WRONG; both must be read. That identification is `Fun`'s, and `Fun` does more than its four sibling donors: **FIVE donors identify hom with proof INDEPENDENTLY** — `Terminal`, `Cartesian`, `HasIndexedProducts`, `IsIndexedProduct` and `Fun` — each rejected under `Constraint uh < up` against controls naming a hom and an object family at those very levels, so no single one is "the" cause. The book numbers Proposition 1 and none of the constructions or remarks, so the catalog ids are names, not book numbering. **THE ABSTRACT PROPOSITION (Structure/SlicedInverse.v and its satellite).** `Sliced G a : (A ̸ a) ⟶ (X ̸ G a)` and `Cosliced G a`, Mac Lane's `G↓a` and `a↓G` on `Construction/Slice.v`'s `Slice` and `Coslice` (an object `(d; h)` goes to `(G d; fmap[G] h)`, both actions read back at `eq_refl`); `RightAdjointRightInverse S` — a right adjoint `rari_right`, `rari_adj : S ⊣ rari_right`, the Leibniz object equation `rari_obj c : S (rari_right c) = c` and `rari_counit c : counit c ≈ id_cast (rari_obj c)`, `Adjunction/LeftInverse.v`'s design crux one parameter over, and in fact `LeftAdjointLeftInverse` with the adjoint moved into the parameter: the satellite's `rari_lali` and `lali_rari` are field-for-field terms whose two round trips hold at `eq_refl` (record eta). The pointwise cores take ONE downstairs (co)equalizer and ONE (co)universal arrow at the one slice object it supplies: `sliced_equalizer` (with `Faithful G`, the lift `sliced_eq_arrow` of the couniversal arrow at `(S; s)` is an equalizer of `f` and `g`, Mac Lane's `Lt : Ls ⟶ x`) and `cosliced_coequalizer`, proved directly (the op route would need a transport functor, `Slice (A^op) a` and `(Coslice A a)^op` orienting the triangle oppositely; argued, not measured). The book forms: `equalizers_from_sliced_right_adjoints`, `equalizers_from_sliced_RARI` (Proposition 1, quoted verbatim in the header: a faithful `G : C ⟶ D`, equalizers in `D` and a right-adjoint-right-inverse of every `G↓x` give `C` equalizers), `coequalizers_from_sliced_left_adjoints`, and the satellite's `coequalizers_from_sliced_LARI` over `Theory/Equivalence/Strict.v`'s existing `LeftAdjointRightInverse` — the dual, so `maclane:V.9:remark2`'s first clause is delivered abstractly here and the rest of #458 is not. **WHERE EACH HYPOTHESIS IS SPENT, MEASURED**: the right-inverse clause is not consumed by Proposition 1 (its body names `rari_right` and `rari_adj`, never `rari_obj` or `rari_counit`, and the theorem it applies has no right-inverse hypothesis), nor are whole adjoints (one couniversal arrow, obtained from the counit by `Adjunction/Determination.v`'s `adj_counit_couniversal`); faithfulness is spent once per variance, on the fork equation — `sliced_desc` and `cosliced_desc`, the existence AND the uniqueness of the mediator, close under `Proof using E U` and take no `Faithful` argument (`About`), while `sliced_fork` under `Proof using E U` is refused, "The following section variable is used but not declared: GF." (pinned). What the clause buys is `rari_preserves`: `G` carries the lifted equalizer onto an equalizer of `fmap[G] f` and `fmap[G] g`, its object `S` up to the Leibniz `rari_over`, with `equalizers_from_sliced_RARI_preserved` and the satellite's dual `lari_preserves`. **FAITHFULNESS CANNOT BE DROPPED**: `prop1_needs_faithfulness` and `prop1_dual_needs_faithfulness` refute both statements with that hypothesis deleted, quantified over all `A`, `X` and `G` at one universe instance, at `Erase Parallel : Parallel ⟶ _1` — every slice (coslice) of `Parallel` has the terminal (initial) object `(a; id)`, so `erase_slice_RARI` (`erase_coslice_LARI`) exists; `_1` has equalizers and coequalizers (`One_HasEqualizers`, `One_HasCoequalizers`, annotated `@{o h}` because unannotated the first minimizes to `HasEqualizers@{u Set} 1`); the pair `par_arrow_one`, `par_arrow_two` has no fork (`parallel_pair_unforked`, `Parallel_no_equalizers`); and `Erase_Parallel_not_faithful`. The header reads the hypothesis against topological functors (nLab, "topological concrete category"; Adámek, Herrlich and Strecker, Theorem 21.3): a sliced right adjoint is the universal lift of ONE map, the right-inverse clause is the EXISTENCE equation `U(T) = X` of an initial lift, and uniqueness (amnesticity) is a separate condition that a chosen right-adjoint-right-inverse does not supply (argued, not built). **PTop (Instance/Top/Prop.v): #1328's item 1, at the path #1328 suggested, beside `Instance/Top.v` and not in its place (`Top` and its consumers are unchanged).** A `PTop@{o}` is a setoid of points with `POpen : (pt_carrier → Prop) → Prop` and five axioms; continuity `PCont` is a proposition, so `PMor@{o} : PTop@{o} → PTop@{o} → Type@{o}` puts the homs at the points' universe, where Test/ProbeStoneCech455.v's N6 refuses `Top`'s `ContinuousMorphism`; `PTopCat@{o so} : Category@{so o o}` and `PForget@{o so} : PTopCat@{o so} ⟶ Sets@{o so}` land in the SAME `Sets` whose objects are the point setoids, so Instance/Top/Forgetful.v's wall does not arise and the sliced adjunctions are `Adjunction` records (`PForget_fobj`, `PForget_fmap` at `eq_refl`; `PForget_Faithful`). **THE UNION AXIOM TAKES A PROP-VALUED FAMILY OF OPENS, AND WHY, MEASURED BOTH WAYS**: under (a), unions over an index type at the points' universe (`p455_TopP`'s form), the subspace's union is witnessed by (index, open) pairs whose type reads back at `Type@{max(Set+1,o)}`, refused as a union index at `o := Set` ("Cannot enforce Set+1 <= Set") and accepted under `Set < o`, and deriving (b) from (a) is refused at `Set` the same way; under (b), `popen_union` for any family `F : (X → Prop) → Prop`, `PSub` is accepted at `PTop@{Set}` with an empty block and (a) follows at EVERY index universe (`popen_union_indexed@{o i}`, empty block, the form Exercise 7.32's unions use); (b) is not shown strictly stronger than (a) at `Set`, only the direct derivation being refused there; both refusals are pinned. The cost of `Prop` is the usual one: membership in an open eliminates only into propositions (`ex` where `Top` has a Σ), and no constant of the two files eliminates it into data. **THE CONSTRUCTIONS (Instance/Top/Subspace.v).** `PSub X S h` along an ARBITRARY setoid map `h`, not only an inclusion, with the book's opens verbatim (`PSub_open`, at `eq_refl`: `ex (fun U => POpen X U /\ ∀ s, V s <-> U (h s))`) and its union witnessed by the union of ALL the witnessing opens, a Prop-valued family, so no choice is made; `psub_universal`, the universal property over ARBITRARY spaces `Z` mapping in, both directions — the issue's Reviewer line, which is the book's own remark on p. 133 — with `psub_lift` its book form. Exercise 7.32 at a subset given by a predicate: `ex732_def` (a set is open iff it is `B ∩ Y` for an open `B`) at `eq_refl`, `ex732_part1` (`Y` is open, `B` the whole space), `ex732_part2` (Definition 7.25's three axioms, unions indexed at any universe), `ex732_part3` (the inclusion is continuous). `PQuot X T q` along an arbitrary map, its opens those with open preimage AND respecting `T`'s equality — the setoid discipline's addition, the pairing `Instance/Top.v`'s `CP_open` and `Instance/Top/Wedge.v`'s `wedge_open` already make — with `pquot_universal` over arbitrary `Z` mapping out and `pquot_desc`. - **Instance/Top/Quotient.v**, **Instance/Top/Quotient/Pairs.v** (probe `Test/ProbeCollapse459.v`): Mac Lane §V.9, read from the page images — the collapse of a subset to a point (book p. 134, PDF p. 143; `maclane:V.9:construction5`) and the category of pairs with the quotient as a left adjoint (book pp. 134–135, PDF pp. 143–144; `maclane:V.9:construction6`), issue #459 — **Construction 5 over the tree's Type-valued `Top` in both of the book's readings of "coequalizer": as a universal arrow to the diagonal (a colimit), for EVERY subset closed under the points' equality, the empty one included, at the apex (X ⊔ {∗})/(A ∼ ∗), and for every subset with a point at the elementary apex; and in the elementary form of book p. 64's display (6), the record `IsWideCoequalizer`, for every subset; with the tree's first inhabitant of `HasWideCoequalizers` beside it. Construction 6 as an `Adjunction` record `PairQuotient ⊣ PointPair` between a new category of pairs and Instance/Top/Homotopy.v's pointed spaces `Top_pointed`, whose value at every pair IS Construction 5's colimit — so under the universal-arrow reading the two constructions agree at every A, and under the elementary reading they part at ⟨∅, ∅⟩, an empty family the book does not treat**. The book numbers neither construction, so the catalog ids are names. Its text, from the page images: "Another coequalizer is the space X/A obtained from the space X by collapsing the subset A to a point. It is the coequalizer [a diagram of the arrows a, …, a′ from * to X, followed by X → X/A] of the set of all the arrows sending the one point space * to one of the points a ∈ A. It is used in homotopy theory. If we consider the category Top^(2) whose objects are pairs ⟨X, A⟩ (a space X with a subset A) and whose arrows ⟨X, A⟩ → ⟨X′, A′⟩ are continuous maps X → X′ sending A to A′, then the definition of X/A, for Y a pointed topological space, reads: Top_*(X/A, Y) = Top^(2)(⟨X, A⟩, ⟨Y, *⟩). Thus ⟨X, A⟩ ↦ X/A is left adjoint to the functor Y ↦ ⟨Y, *⟩ which sends each pointed space to the pair ⟨Y, *⟩." It says "coequalizer", not "wide coequalizer", and "=", not "≅"; it says nothing about A = ∅ and puts no non-emptiness condition on Top^(2). Its "coequalizer" is §III.3's (book pp. 64–65, PDF pp. 73–74, read from the page images), which reads two ways. Mac Lane DEFINES the coequalizer of a pair elementarily, display (6) on p. 64: an arrow u : b → e with uf = ug, through which every h : b → c with hf = hg factors uniquely. He then says that a coequalizer "can be interpreted as a universal arrow", p. 65 reads it as "just a universal arrow from ⟨f, g⟩ to the functor Δ", and "Coequalizers of any set of maps from a to b are defined in the same way". The two readings agree on every nonempty set of maps. At the empty set they differ, and the book does not treat that case: the universal arrow — a colimit over the shape that has the domain * as a vertex, Structure/Coequalizer/Wide.v's `WideCoequalizer` — is the coproduct a ⊔ b, here X ⊔ *, while the elementary form — (6) extended, that file's record `IsWideCoequalizer`, the reading its header adopts — is b, here X (that file's `wide_coround_trip_needs_point` and header). The universal-arrow reading is the one p. 135 needs, since Top_*(X/A, Y) takes X/A pointed. **OVER THE TYPE-VALUED `Top`, NOT `PTopCat`**: both constructions are stated over Instance/Top.v's `Top@{h o}`, and #457's Prop-valued `PTopCat` is not used, by the criterion of the maintainer's decision of 2026-09-24, which takes the Prop-valued encoding where the Type-valued `Top` is walled: both scouts' prototypes compiled over `Top` with no universe wall on either construction's path, and the pointed spaces the adjunction needs exist over `Top` only (`Top_pointed`; no pointed category over `PTopCat` is built). **CONSTRUCTION 5 (Quotient.v)**: `Top_collapse X I p` collapses the image of any family `p : I → X` of points — two points are identified when they are equal or both lie in the SATURATED image `collapse_image`, so nothing is asked of `p` — with the quotient topology `TQuot` of Instance/Top/Subspace/TypeValued.v, the points' equality being `collapse_rel` at `eq_refl` (`Top_collapse_equiv`); X/A is a `TopSpace@{o}`, an object of the same `Top@{h o}` as X. `collapse_family X I p i := top_point X (p i)` is the point-inclusion `Point_Top ~> X`, and `collapse_family_coequalizer` proves `collapse_proj : X ~> X/A` an elementary `IsWideCoequalizer` (Structure/Coequalizer/Wide.v's record) of that family for EVERY family, the empty one included, over arbitrary spaces mapping out, the mediator being the competing map itself on points (`collapse_desc_map_points`, `eq_refl`). Mac Lane's subset form: a subset is a Type-valued predicate `A : X → Type`, `Top_collapse_sub X A` is X/A, `collapse_sub_family X A` the book's "set of all the arrows sending the one point space * to one of the points a ∈ A", and `collapse_coequalizer` (the issue's pinned name) Construction 5 in the elementary form, for every subset. The colimit form at this apex, `collapse_colimit` (with `collapse_family_colimit`), takes a point of A: it is Structure/Coequalizer/Wide.v's round trip `is_wide_coequalizer_colimit` from the elementary record, which takes one, and that file's `wide_coround_trip_needs_point` proves the point cannot be dropped from the round trip in general, and Pairs.v's `empty_colimit_not_elementary` that it cannot at this apex at ⟨∅, ∅⟩; the colimit itself needs no point (Pairs.v's `pquot_wide_coequalizer_colimit`, below). `collapse_proj_epic` comes from `wide_coequalizer_epic`; and at the empty subset the elementary X/∅ is X (`collapse_empty_iso : X/∅ ≅ X`, through `wide_empty_id_IsWideCoequalizer`). **SMALL WIDE COEQUALIZERS OF `Top` (Quotient.v)**: `wcoeq_rel`, the relation a family of setoid maps generates (all the pairs `(f_i a, f_j a)`; the wide analogue of Instance/Sets/Coequalizer.v's `coeq_rel`), its quotient setoid `WSetsCoeq` and `twcoeq_obj := TQuot` on it give `Top_HasWideCoequalizers_small : HasWideCoequalizers@{i h h} Top@{h o}` at every index universe `i` at or below the points' `o`, its object read back at `eq_refl` (`Top_wide_coequalizer_obj`) — the class's FIRST inhabitant (a word `git grep` of `HasWideCoequalizers` over the `.v` files at master 386a2270 finds only its declaring file); `collapse_iso_generic` compares the direct collapse with the generic wide coequalizer of its family by `wide_coequalizer_unique`, the identity on points both ways at `eq_refl` (`collapse_iso_generic_to`, `collapse_iso_generic_from`). No `Sets` instance is packaged, though `WSetsCoeq` is the quotient it would need. **THE CATEGORY OF PAIRS AND THE ADJUNCTION (Pairs.v)**: `PairTop` is a space with a Type-valued predicate on its points closed under their equality (`pair_sub_proper`), `PairMap` a continuous map carrying subset into subset, the hom-setoid `Top`'s own on the underlying maps as Instance/Top/Homotopy.v's `PointedMap_Setoid` is, and `Top_pairs : Category@{h h h}` is Top^(2), the shape of `Top_pointed`. `PointPair : Top_pointed ⟶ Top_pairs` sends Y to ⟨Y, *⟩, the subset `y ≈ y0` (`PointPair_sub`, `eq_refl`); `PairQuotient : Top_pairs ⟶ Top_pointed` sends ⟨X, A⟩ to X/A pointed at the new point. `pairs_quotient_iso X Y` is the book's display, an `Isomorphism` in `Sets` (its "=" is refused at `eq_refl` as an equation of hom types, the probe's N12) whose `to` restricts along the inclusion and whose `from` sends the new point to the basepoint, continuous by `TQuot`'s universal property; `pairs_quotient_adjunction` (the issue's pinned name) is `Build_Adjunction'` on it, both naturality squares pointwise reflexivity, with the unit x ↦ `Some x`, the counit `Some y` ↦ y and `None` ↦ the basepoint, and `adj` IS `pairs_quotient_iso`, all at `eq_refl` (`pairs_quotient_unit_eval`, `pairs_quotient_counit_some`, `pairs_quotient_counit_none`, `pairs_quotient_adj_is`). every colimit of that family has a point, the image of * (`collapse_colimit_point`), the component * → X/A of the universal arrow, the basepoint that Top_*(X/A, Y) presupposes; it is the pushout X ⊔_A ∗ in `Top` (`pquot_pushout`, of the inclusion of the points of A, carrying the discrete topology, against the map to the point), its apex `pquot_space X` at `eq_refl` (`pquot_pushout_apex`), and the colimit's universal property is proved through the pushout's mediator `pquot_po_med`; - **Instance/Top/Circle.v**, **Instance/Top/Solenoid.v**, **Instance/Top/Solenoid/Presentations.v** (probe `Test/ProbeSolenoid410.v`): Mac Lane §V.1 Construction 3 (book p. 111, PDF p. 120, read from the page image; `maclane:V.1:construction3`), with the second half of Riehl §3.6 Example 3.6.3 (printed p. 116, PDF p. 136, read from the page image; `riehl:3.6:example3`), issue #410 — **the p-adic solenoid as the limit of the tower of circles under the p-fold wrapping map, in #259's Type-valued `Top` under the issue's pinned name `solenoid_limit`, its topology not posited but characterised — by its universal property (a map into it is continuous iff every composite with a projection is) and as the coarsest topology making the legs continuous — its points #408's matching strings at `eq_refl`, the underlying-set functor preserving the limit; the same limit over #457's Prop-valued `PTopCat` by #458's recipe (`PTop_solenoid_limit`); the circle R/Z over the standard library's CONSTRUCTIVE Cauchy reals, with no axiom; and Riehl's box: the circle group's tower in `Ab` and the circle's towers of spaces have one underlying tower, the group solenoid sits on the same strings, its fibre over the base point is the p-adic integers as an abelian group, and the p-fold map is a covering, evenly covered neighbourhoods with p sheets, in `PTopCat` and in the Type-valued `Top`**. The book's text, from the page image: "Again, in Top, take each object F_n to be a circle S^1, and each arrow f_n : S^1 → S^1 to be the continuous map wrapping the domain circle S^1 uniformly p times around the codomain circle. The inverse limit set L then becomes a topological space when we introduce just those open sets in L necessary to make all the functions μ_n : L → S^1 continuous. This L is the limit space in Top; it is known as the p-adic solenoid."; Riehl's: "For instance, consider the diagram ω^op → Top whose objects are circles S^1 and in which each generating map is the "pth power map," the covering map that wraps the domain circle uniformly p times around the codomain circle: … The inverse limit defines the p-adic solenoid." Neither page says which model of the circle it means, and the two pages give the one diagram. **THE CIRCLE (Circle.v), R/Z OVER THE CONSTRUCTIVE REALS**: the reals already in the tree are the standard library's classical `R`, which carries `sig_forall_dec` and `functional_extensionality_dep` (`Print Assumptions` of Instance/Top/Interval.v's `I_Top`); the circle is built instead on the standard library's constructive Cauchy reals `CReal` (Reals/Cauchy/ConstructiveCauchyReals.v), nLab's "modulated" Cauchy reals, whose order `CRealLt` is Set-valued and whose equality `CRealEq` is a proposition. `RLine_setoid` is `CReal` under `CRealEq`; `Circle_setoid` is `CReal` under `circ_eq`, two reals being one point when their difference is an integer, the integer KEPT AS DATA (`{ k : Z & x - y == k }`), because the Type-valued `Top`'s opens are Type-valued predicates and the forward half of `circle_open_balls` moves a point of an open along an integer translate inside one, which needs the integer as a term. `RLine` (Type-valued metric opens `ropen`, closed rational balls `rball`) and `PRLine` (Prop-valued, `propen`) are the line, and the circle is its QUOTIENT along `circ_q` in each category — `Circle` is Instance/Top/Subspace/TypeValued.v's `TQuot`, `PCircle` Instance/Top/Subspace.v's `PQuot` — with `circle_open_balls` (`iffT`) and `pcircle_open_balls` (`iff`) identifying each quotient topology with the circle's own ball topology `cball`, both directions, with no hypothesis. The p-fold maps `wrap p : Circle ~{Top}~> Circle` and `pwrap p` in `PTopCat` descend along the quotients (`tquot_desc`, `pquot_desc`), continuous because multiplication by p carries a ball of radius e/p into one of radius e (`rball_mul`); their underlying map IS `circ_mul p`, x ↦ p·x (`wrap_map`, `pwrap_map`, `eq_refl`), which on R/Z is Mac Lane's wrapping map and Riehl's p-th power map at once (under x ↦ e^(2πix), an identification recorded as background only: the tree has no complex numbers). `wrap_one` and `pwrap_one` give the identity up to `≈` at p = 1, and `circle_half_not_zero` refutes 1/2 ≈ 0. The equality's `Prop` mirror `circ_peq`, the implication back `circ_eq_of_peq` — the integer recomputed by rounding, `cround`, the floor of a rational approximation of the real plus 1/2, with no choice principle — the resulting `circ_PropEquiv`, and `circle_lift_iso` (the identity maps between the lifted `Circle_setoid@{o}` and `Circle_setoid@{h}`) sit in Circle.v, moved there from Presentations.v on review. The standard library's header of ConstructiveCauchyReals.v says the module "is not meant to be imported directly" and "is experimental and likely to change in future releases"; its abstract interface does not name `CReal`, so the three modules are imported directly under the tree's `Coq.Reals` prefix — a forward-compatibility risk on Rocq master, which CI does not test, disclosed in Circle.v's header. **THE TOWERS (Solenoid.v)**: `EndoTower X w`, the tower … → X → X → X of an endomorphism `w` in ANY category, a functor out of `Omega^op` in Instance/Rng/Zp.v's `res_hom` idiom, with `endo_step` (the generating arrow IS `id ∘ w`, `eq_refl`) and `EndoTower_map` (a functor carries the tower of `w` to the tower of `fmap w`, `≈` in `Functor_Setoid` with identity components); `UCircleTower p` in `Sets`, `CircleTower p` in `Top` (Mac Lane's tower, `CircleTower_step` at `eq_refl`) and `PCircleTower p` in `PTopCat`, with `PCircleTower_points : PForget ◯ PCircleTower p ≈ UCircleTower p`. Statements write `omega_step n` where Instance/Sets/InverseLimit.v writes `tower_step n` (one term, `tower_step_is_omega_step`): three of `tower_step`'s universes carry that file's section block, and a closed universe list cannot bind them ("unbound", the probe's N6). **THE SOLENOID IN THE TYPE-VALUED `Top`, THE ISSUE'S CATEGORY AND ITS PINNED NAME**: the generic initial topology, in the two Type-valued forms measured, does not reach this category at the points' universe. For a nat-indexed family into `Top`, both forms — W1, quantifying over all families of predicates on the points that contain the subbasic opens, with no closure axioms asked of them, and W2, a union of subbasic opens indexed by the opens of the factors — are refused at the points' universe ("Cannot enforce o < o") and accepted one universe up, both pinned in the probe (N2, N3) against the controls one universe up (`p410_init_family_up`, `p410_init_union_up`). The solenoid's topology avoids the wall: `sopen p` quantifies over a stage n and a rational radius e > 0, never over opens, so `Solenoid p : TopSpace@{o}` sits at the points' universe — a predicate on the matching strings `SolPoints p` is open when every point s of it has a stage n and a radius e such that every string within e of s on the circle's balls, at every stage j ≤ n, is in it. The Reviewer line — "the topology on the limit must be characterised by its universal property, not merely posited" — is MET: `solenoid_universal`, a setoid map from ANY space into the points is continuous iff every composite with a projection is (`iffT`); `solenoid_coarsest`, every topology on the points (given by the closure properties of Instance/Top.v's `TopSpace`) in which each projection is continuous contains every open of `Solenoid p`; and with `sol_leg_cont` (the preimage of every open of the circle along a projection is in `sopen`) it is exactly the coarsest topology making the legs continuous, Mac Lane's "just those open sets in L necessary". The content is `sol_lift_cont`: the preimage of an open along a map is the union, over its points, of finite intersections (`open_bounded_inter`) of preimages of the open interiors of the circle's balls (Circle.v's `cint_open`). `solenoid_limit p : Limit (CircleTower p)`, its mediator `sol_med` the tuple of a competing cone's legs, uniqueness pointwise; `solenoid_forget_preserves : IsLimitCone (FCone Top_Forget (sol_cone p))` — at this tower `Top_Forget`, into the lifted `Sets@{h hs}`, preserves the limit cone, while Instance/Top/Forgetful.v's header records cone-level preservation for that lifted functor as "neither claimed nor concluded" in general, which stands. `solenoid_limit` is the first `Limit` over the Type-valued `Top` in the tree: a `git grep -n -w Limit` of the tracked `.v` files outside `Test/` at master afcac4ee, read for constants whose type is a `Limit` of a diagram into `Top`, finds none — every `Limit` built under Instance/Top/ is over `PTopCat`, at a generic category or at Instance/Top/Complete/ConeComma.v's countermodel, and `Top`'s one registered limit-like structure is Instance/Top.v's `Top_Terminal`, a `Terminal`. **THE SOLENOID IN `PTopCat`, BY #458'S RECIPE, WHICH IS RIEHL'S SENTENCE**: `PTop_solenoid_limit p` IS Instance/Top/Complete.v's `PTop_Limit_lift` applied to #408's matching-strings limit `Sets_tower_Limit` of the underlying tower; its characterisations are #458's theorems at this tower — `PTop_solenoid_universal` (`pinit_universal`), `PTop_solenoid_coarsest` (`pinit_weakest`), `PTop_solenoid_open_forced` (the opens of EVERY limiting cone over the tower are the initial topology of its legs, `PTop_limit_open_iff_initial`) and `PTop_solenoid_forget_preserves` (`PForget_PreservesLimitCone`). Over #259's Type-valued `Top` the wall is the functor, not the relation: C must land among the point setoids, the objects of `Sets@{o so}`, and a functor `Top@{h o} ⟶ Sets@{o so}` is refused ("Cannot enforce o = … because o < h <= …", the probe's N1: `Top`'s homs sit at `h` above the points and a functor cannot lower the hom level, the reason Instance/Top/Forgetful.v gives for landing its underlying-set functor in `Sets@{h so}`); one universe up the functor and an `Adjunction` record with `Sets@{h so}` are formable (controls), but not one whose right adjoint is Forgetful.v's `Top_Discrete`, whose domain must be the point setoids (N2, "Cannot enforce … = h because h < …"). The relation is not the obstacle: its Type-valued forms — a Σ over Type-valued subsets, the quasi-component form, connectedness over discrete targets — are refused at `Type@{o}` ("Cannot enforce o < o because o = o", N3–N5) and accepted at `Type@{h}` under `o < h`, while a Prop-valued component relation over `TopSpace@{o}`, its neighbourhoods Prop-truncated opens, is accepted under the closed list `@{o}`, `About` reading back an empty block on Rocq 9.1 (the probe's control `tcomp_rel_prop`). Over `PTopCat` the opens are Prop-valued, the homs sit at the points' universe, and every relation below is a proposition. **CONNECTEDNESS, PROP-VALUED (Components.v)**: `LocConstOn X W φ` (a Prop-valued φ locally constant on the subset W), `PConnectedSub X W` (every such φ constant on W) and `PConnected X`; `comp_rel X x y`, x and y in a common connected subset, an equivalence relation constructively (`point_connected`, `union_connected`), whose classes are the connected components; `CompSet X` the points under `comp_rel`, `comp_PropEquiv` its equality the proposition `comp_rel` itself. The locally-constant form is the one the adjunction needs, its transpose taking φ z := the equality of `g x` and `g z` as a proposition, where a `bool` indicator would need a decidable equality on the target. The bridges to the other two forms are delivered for subsets and spaces — `connected_no_separation` and `PConnected_Sep` (two disjoint opens covering the space do not split it, `PConnectedSep`), `connected_bool_constant` and `PConnected_Bool` (every continuous map into `PBool` is constant, `PConnectedBool`) — and their CONVERSES ARE NOT DELIVERED: each needs a decision of φ at every point, excluded middle (informative for the `bool` form); classically the three agree, and nLab's connected-space page warns that constructively they "no longer need to be equivalent". **LOCAL CONNECTEDNESS AND THE TWO CATEGORIES**: `PLocConn X`, nLab's and Wikipedia's definition (every open neighbourhood of a point contains a connected open one); `Lconn`, the full subcategory of `PTopCat` on it (`Lconn_Sub` over Instance/Top/Separation.v's `PFullSub`), and `PSets`, the full subcategory of `Sets` on Instance/Sets/Propositional.v's `PropEquivObj` (`PSetsSub`), both `Category@{so o o}` and pinned by hand as Instance/Top/Hausdorff.v pins `Haus` (`Sub@{so o o o so o so}` and `Sub@{so o so o so o so}`) (CORRECTION (#1349): #469 built the same category again as Instance/Sets/Propositional/Full.v's `PropSets_sub` and `PropSets`; on the maintainer's decision to unify them, Components.v now requires Full.v and defines `PSetsSub` and `PSets` as those two, so the hand pin of `PSets` is Full.v's, `About` reading the same blocks for both names as before; Components.v's `Require` closure is 119 modules, itself and Full.v included, by `Print Libraries`). **MAC LANE'S SET, READ AS THE PROPOSITIONAL SETS, AND WHY**: the tree's `Sets` has a Type-valued `≈`, `comp_rel` is a proposition, and a proposition is not eliminated into a type — extracting a Type-valued witness from `comp_rel X x y` is refused (N6), and so is turning `inhabited (pmap g x ≈ pmap g y)` into the equality itself (N7, "Incorrect elimination of "HR" in the inductive type "inhabited": the return type has sort "Type" while it should be SProp or Prop"), while through a `PropEquiv` of the target it is accepted (Lib/Setoid/Propositional.v's `pequiv_elim_inhabited`, the control). The obstruction is in the statement, not the proof, and it is MEASURED: `components_on_all_Sets_unsquashes` shows that ANY left adjoint of the discrete functor `LDisc : Sets ⟶ Lconn` yields `inhabited (∀ Q : Type@{o}, inhabited Q → Q)` — the unit at the indiscrete two-point space is continuous into a discrete space, so its two values are only merely equal, and the transpose of the identity into the two-point setoid whose `true ≈ false` is Q (`SquashSetoid`, continuous as soon as Q is merely inhabited, `squash_id_cont`) unsquashes Q — whence functional choice for relations between types at `o` (`unsquash_choice`); `unsquash_Untruncate` and its converse `Untruncate_unsquash` identify that principle, up to truncation, with the tree's own hypothesis `Untruncate` (Instance/Sets/Classifier/OneLevel.v's: every impredicative truncation at level `o` inverts), so any such adjunction yields `inhabited Untruncate@{o}` (`components_on_all_Sets_Untruncate`) (CORRECTION (#1349): `SquashSetoid`, with `squash_rel`, `squash_sym` and `squash_trans`, moved to Full.v unchanged, and `unsquash_Untruncate` and `Untruncate_unsquash` are now transparent definitions derived from Full.v's `untr_of_choice` and `choice_of_untr`, the #469 statements of the same links). And the hypothesis suffices: `components_left_adjoint_discrete_Sets : Untruncate@{o} → components_functor_Sets ⊣ LDisc`, the literal reading, with `components_functor_Sets : Lconn ⟶ Sets`, its transposes again the identity on points at `eq_refl` (`adj_Sets_to_points`, `adj_Sets_from_points`) and the hypothesis spent once, in `comp_respect_U` (a continuous map into ANY discrete space is constant on components). So Mac Lane's Set is read UNCONDITIONALLY as `PSets`, the reading the concrete algebraic categories take (the size note in Structure/Complete.v's header), and LITERALLY as `Sets` under `Untruncate`, whose truncation is necessary (it has no axiom-free inhabitant in the tree and follows from informative excluded middle, OneLevel.v's `untruncate_of_IEM`): the one deviation from the book's statement beyond the `PTopCat` encoding, lifted at `Sets` under that hypothesis. **C AND D, AND THE ADJUNCTION**: `image_connected` (continuous images of connected subsets are connected) gives `CompTop : PTopCat ⟶ PSets`, the components functor on ALL spaces, and `components_functor : Lconn ⟶ PSets` is `CompTop` after the inclusion. D is Instance/Top/Complete.v's `PDisc`, not a second discrete functor: `LDisc : Sets ⟶ Lconn` has `PDisc`'s object and arrow parts (`LDisc_PDisc_obj`, `LDisc_PDisc_fmap`, `eq_refl`) and its three functor laws, with `pdisc_locconn` (a discrete space is locally connected), and `PSetsDisc : PSets ⟶ Lconn`, Mac Lane's D, is `LDisc` after the inclusion of `PSets`. `components_left_adjoint_discrete : components_functor ⊣ PSetsDisc` is Theory/Adjunction.v's `Build_Adjunction'` from `comp_adj_iso`, a hom-set bijection that is the identity on points both ways: `comp_respect` (a continuous map into a discrete space on a propositional set is constant on components) and `comp_cont` (in a locally connected space a map constant on components is continuous into a discrete space, the preimage of an open being the union of the connected open sets meeting it). Local connectedness is used once, at the whole space, for a connected open neighbourhood of each point (read off `comp_cont`'s proof), so the adjunction would hold on the larger class of spaces whose every point has a connected open neighbourhood; the book's class is kept. This is the leftmost adjunction of nLab's quadruple Π₀ ⊣ Δ ⊣ Γ ⊣ ∇ on locally connected spaces; its categorical twin, Mac Lane's §IV.2 Exercise 9 (book p. 90, the components of a category left adjoint to the discrete functor), is Instance/Cat/Components.v's `Components_Disc_Adjunction : Pi0 ⊣ Cat_Disc`. **RIGHT ADJOINTS PRESERVE EQUALIZERS (Equalizer.v)**: `right_adjoint_PreservesEqualizers (A : F ⊣ U) : PreservesEqualizers U`, Structure/Limit/FromProducts.v's elementary predicate (the one #416's `continuous_from_products_equalizers` consumes; at master 2640b965 it occurs only in its own file, as a hypothesis, by `git grep -w` over the `.v` files outside `Test/`), by direct transposition — a fork of the image pair transposes to a fork in C (`from_adj_nat_r`), descends through the equalizer and transposes back (`to_adj_nat_r`, `from_adj_comp_law`); and `not_PreservesEqualizers_no_left_adjoint`, the contrapositive as the refutation Mac Lane's parenthesis names. THE BOOKS: Mac Lane, after the remark that for "other authors (Barr-Wells [1985]), "triplable" means only that K be an equivalence of categories": "However, here is an easy example when K is not an isomorphism, and not even an equivalence. The forgetful functor G : Top → Set has a left adjoint D which assigns to each set X the discrete topological space (all subsets open in X), for the identity arrow η_X : X → GDX is trivially universal from the object X to the functor G. This adjunction ⟨D, G, η, …⟩ : Set ⇀ Top defines on Set the monad I = ⟨I, 1, 1⟩ which is the identity (identity functor, identity as unit and as multiplication). The I-algebras in Set are just the sets, so the comparison functor Top → Top^I = Set is in this case the given forgetful functor G." Awodey: "An example of a right adjoint that is not monadic is the forgetful functor from posets, U : Pos → Sets. Its left adjoint F is the discrete poset functor. For any set X, therefore, one has as the unit the identity function X = UF(X). The reader can easily show that the Eilenberg-Moore category for T = 1_Sets is then just Sets itself." Neither page gives the argument that the comparison is not an equivalence; the files supply one. THE READING IMPLEMENTED: the page prints the comparison's target as "Top^I = Set"; the I-algebras live in Set, so the target taken is `EilenbergMoore` of the induced monad on `Sets`, and "= Set" is read as an equivalence between it and `Sets`, an algebra keeping its structure map, which is ≈ id and need not be id (#467's `A_id_ne_A_true` exhibits two algebras of `IdSM` on one carrier); "not an isomorphism, and not even an equivalence" covers both readings of monadic the page names, and `Monadic` (Monad/Comparison.v) is the Barr–Wells one. WHY `PTopCat`: over the tree's Type-valued `Top` the discrete adjunction is not an `Adjunction` record at any universe assignment (Instance/Top/Forgetful.v's header; `Test/ProbeUniversalArrows312.v` pins the refusal), so its induced monad and comparison functor cannot be formed there, and by the maintainer's decision of 2026-09-24 such issues are built on `PTopCat`, where Instance/Top/Complete.v's `PDisc_PForget : PDisc ⊣ PForget` is one (#458). THE IDENTITY MONAD, Monad/Identity.v: `IdMonad C : Monad Id[C]` at every `Category@{o h h}`, the constructor `Build_Monad` with every field given, as Monad/Eilenberg/Moore/Limit/Examples.v's `IdSM` is on `Sets` only, with two universe levels and an empty constraint list on Rocq 9.1.1, Coq 8.20.1 and 8.19.2 alike (by `About` on each); of the tree's earlier identity monads, Monad/Strong.v's `Id_Monad`, a section-local `Program Instance`, has 3, 5 and 17 universe levels on the three versions (#467's measurement), so that no explicit instance of it compiles on all three, `IdSM` is at `Sets` only, and `Adjunction_Induced_Monad Adjunction_Id`, the monad behind Monad/Monadicity/Examples.v's `identity_monadic`, has the functor Id ◯ Id; its functor, unit and multiplication read back as the identity at `eq_refl` (`IdMonad_fobj`, `IdMonad_fmap`, `IdMonad_ret`, `IdMonad_join`), every algebra's structure map is ≈ id (`IdMonad_alg_id`), and `IdMonad_EM_equivalence` makes the forgetful functor of its Eilenberg–Moore category an equivalence with `EM_Free` as quasi-inverse, the legs of its unit isomorphism `id` at `eq_refl` (`IdMonad_EM_unit_iso_id`). MAC LANE'S EXAMPLE, Instance/Top/Monadicity.v: `PDiscT := PForget ◯ PDisc` and `PDiscMonad := Adjunction_Induced_Monad PDisc_PForget`; "identity functor" is `PDiscT_fobj` and `PDiscT_fmap`, "identity as unit and as multiplication" `PDiscMonad_ret` and `PDiscMonad_join`, and as functions the four data fields are those of `IdMonad Sets` (`PDiscT_fields`, `PDiscMonad_fields`); "the identity arrow η_X" is `PDisc_PForget_unit`, and the counit is the identity on points (`PDisc_PForget_counit`), all at `eq_refl`; "which is the identity" is `disc_id_iso`, an isomorphism in `Monads Sets` between (PDiscT; PDiscMonad) and (Id[Sets]; IdMonad Sets) whose morphisms of monads `disc_id_hom` and `id_disc_hom` have `id` as every component at `eq_refl`; as objects of `Monads Sets` the two are refused equal, and so is `PDiscT = Id[Sets]`. THE BOOKS: Mac Lane, "For any ring R with identity, the forgetful functor G: R-Mod→Set … has a left adjoint and so defines a monad ⟨T_R, η, μ⟩ in Set. ## Applied Programming (Theory/Coq/)
Bridges pure theory with practical Coq programming:
- Applicative functors proven via monoidal functors
- Traversable functors with laws
- Monad transformers with coherence conditions — `MonadTransformer` and `MonadTransformerLaws` are in **Monad/Transformer.v**, NOT under `Theory/Coq/`; they are listed here because they belong to this applied layer thematically (CORRECTION (#468): `MonadTransformerLaws` is not a constant of the tree. It sits inside a comment block of Monad/Transformer.v, as it has since e0761772 (2017-05-29): in a scratch file carrying that file's four `Require` lines and the module itself, `Definition x := @MonadTransformerLaws.` is refused with "The reference MonadTransformerLaws was not found in the current environment" and `Locate` prints "No object of basename MonadTransformerLaws", while `Check @MonadTransformer.` is accepted (Rocq 9.1.1). The sentence was inaccurate when written, in CLAUDE.md's Key Files index by ee1ce4fd (2026-08-12; PR #1085, merged 2026-08-13), and came here unchanged with the index by PR #1284 (merged 2026-09-09). `MonadTransformer` is in that file, and since #468 Monad/Morphism/Transformer.v proves its laws at one monad M exactly a morphism of monads M ⟶ T M, `transformer_hom` and `hom_transformer`)
